title: host_of() disagrees with the browser on backslash-userinfo URLs: resolve() releases the secret for 'https://evil.test\@pathlynks.test', which Chromium (WHATWG) navigates to evil.test
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:60-63 host_of uses urllib.parse.urlparse, which treats 'evil.test\\' as userinfo and returns hostname 'pathlynks.test'. WHATWG URL (what Chromium/Playwright implement; verified with node `new URL(...)`): backslash is a path separator in special schemes, so host='evil.test', path='/@pathlynks.test'. Probe: SecretStore(proj(domains=['pathlynks.test']),{'PW':'supersecretvalue'}).resolve('{{SECRET:PW}}','https://evil.test\\@pathlynks.test') RETURNED the value. B3 says scoping is enforced against the current page host; here the page host would be evil.test. Note: 'https://evil.test%2F@pathlynks.test' is consistent on both parsers (host pathlynks.test) and is NOT a leak; the cycle-1 userinfo probe ('a.test@evil.test') was the safe direction. Fix direction (fail closed, two lines): in host_of() return '' when the raw input contains a backslash or when urlparse yields a username/password (any userinfo) â€” an empty host already raises SecretScopeError since AT-001. Add both as tests. T-010 must additionally pass the browser's own page.url (post-navigation) to resolve(), never the step's intended URL. CYCLE-3 RE-CHECK: host_of (secrets.py:73-88) returns '' on any backslash or any urlparse userinfo; resolve() raises SecretScopeError on ''. Cross-checked 35 destinations against node v24 `new URL(...).hostname`: every case where urlparse and WHATWG disagree in the leak direction ('evil.test\@pathlynks.test', 'pathlynks.test@evil.test', 'https:\\pathlynks.test', 'evil.test:@pathlynks.test', '@pathlynks.test', U+2044 userinfo) now returns '' (refused). Remaining disagreements ('pathlynks%2Etest', 'pathlynksï¼Žtest', trailing-space host) are all in the safe direction (refused while the browser would visit the legit host). Pinned by test_at007_backslash_and_userinfo_destinations_fail_closed.

Logged verbatim by the maker to qa/feedback-inbox.md (2026-09-07) and correctly deferred: no ui.md criterion U1-U5 requires case creation from the UI, and its no-fire list already defers run-triggering. Filed so it becomes queued, contract-scoped work rather than inbox prose. Needs a scoping decision first: an add-a-case flow vs an explicit prominent next-step prompt on an empty project. | FIXED 2026-09-07 by unit ui-add-case (both halves of the scoping decision taken: an add-a-case flow AND an empty-state prompt). Checker-verified live on a fresh hostile project: GET /projects/ renders 'No cases yet' + '+ Add the first case', GET /projects//cases/new renders the form prefilled with the project's own base_url, POST /projects//cases persists a real schema.case.Case to projects//cases.jsonl (kind derived, id content-addressed, blank rows dropped and renumbered), after which the prompt is gone and Run tests is a real submit button. Verdict: qa/verdicts/ui-add-case.md. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): The add-a-case route exists in src/autotester/ui/routes_cases.py and the empty-state prompt renders from the project page.

title: Onboarding accepts an allowed_domains value that makes the project permanently unrunnable, and says nothing -- a project whose base_url host is not inside its own allowed_domains fails every run at execution time with a NavigationRefused the user cannot act on, and there is no UI to edit the value afterwards
evidence: Umesh onboarded the ERP project through the UI typing 'all' in Allowed domains, plainly meaning 'allow everything'. The form accepted it verbatim, so projects/erp/project.json holds allowed_domains: ['all'] while base_url is 'https://www.vidysea.com/erp'. The first real run (run-01M1WSZWBP57PNNR9N6DMJMHW6) came back INCONCLUSIVE, scoreboard 'not judged: execution errored', note "NavigationRefused: 'https://www.vidysea.com/erp' is outside allowed domains ['all']" -- i.e. the project could never have tested anything from the moment it was created. Two distinct defects: (1) ui/app.py::onboard_submit does no validation that the project's OWN base_url host falls inside the allowed_domains it is being given, so an obviously self-contradictory project is persisted silently; (2) there is no route anywhere to edit a project's allowed_domains/base_url after onboarding, so a user who gets it wrong once cannot fix it from the UI at all (ui/routes_credentials.py edits .env values only, never project.json). NOT fixed by widening allowed_domains to support a literal 'all'/wildcard: allowed_domains is a documented hard security boundary ('the browser will never navigate outside these', CLAUDE.md + ARCHITECTURE.md security section), and adding an allow-anything escape hatch is a security-model change requiring an explicit decision, not a bug fix. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): _require_reachable_base_url exists in src/autotester/ui/helpers.py and guards the onboarding path.
found_by: umesh+maker (live end-to-end run of the new add-a-case flow)
checker_note: Both halves verified by /checker unit ui-project-edit-and-domain-validation cycle 1. (1) Prevention: POST /onboard with base_url=https://www.vidysea.com/erp + allowed_domains=all returns HTTP 400 naming 'www.vidysea.com' and creates no projects/erp-probe/ directory (re-run live against localhost:8010, not the maker's paste). (2) Recovery: seeded a scratch project in the exact broken state (allowed_domains ['all']), reached GET /projects/chk-broken/edit (200), fixed it via POST (303), and confirmed browser.session.check_destination(project, base_url) then returns 'www.vidysea.com' instead of raising NavigationRefused -- the recovered project passes the REAL navigation gate, not just the validator. Validator proven equal to the boundary: session.check_destination is host_of + Project.allows_domain and _require_reachable_base_url composes the identical pair, so no over-tightening; all four on-disk projects (pathlynks, vidysea-erp, regression-demo, erp) still pass. The wildcard half stays deliberately unfixed and is NOT a residue of this issue: expressing 'allow everything' is a security-boundary widening reserved to Umesh, and the user's actual intent is fully expressible because the error names the exact host to add.

title: A case's auto-generated default rubric is persisted keyed on the case id, but its criterion text derives from case.rationale which is NOT part of that id -- so changing a case's rationale silently keeps grading against the OLD claim forever, with no invalidation path
evidence: Found live while proving the new UI add-a-case flow end to end. stages/run_case_pipeline.py::default_rubric builds its single criterion as f'The evidence is consistent with: {case.rationale or ...}' and the result is saved to projects/<slug>/rubrics/rub_<case_id>.json. Case.compute_id() (schema/case.py) hashes only (project, flow_id, case_class, steps) -- rationale is deliberately excluded, so two cases differing only in rationale are the SAME case id by design. Consequence observed: a case created with rationale 'added by hand from the UI' persisted a rubric whose claim was literally 'The evidence is consistent with: added by hand from the UI'; after the rationale was corrected to None and the case re-created through the real HTTP form (same id, correctly deduped), run-01M1WT69EQFRYZC4NYHEY0FY1Z STILL graded against the stale rubric and FAILed with 'Evidence shows only login page; manual addition not performed' -- a hallucinated criterion, on a screenshot that plainly showed the sign-in page the case actually asked for. Deleting projects/erp/rubrics/rub_case_27256e2a2b8d.json was the only way to recover. The bug is the missing invalidation, not the dedup: either the rubric file should be content-addressed on the claim text it was built from, or load_rubric should regenerate when the stored claim no longer matches the case's current rationale/title. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): Provenance stamping is present in stages/run_case_pipeline.py.
found_by: umesh+maker (live end-to-end run of the new add-a-case flow)
checker_note: Fixed by unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation (verdict qa/verdicts/grade-stale-rubric-invalidation.md, cycle 1). run_case_pipeline.py now stamps Provenance(produced_by=GENERATOR, note=claim) on every generated rubric and regenerates via is_stale_default() when the recorded claim no longer matches claim_of(case). Checker re-derived: 12 independent false-positive attacks on the overwrite guard all returned False; the genuinely stale case returns True; no churn on an unchanged claim. Residual filed as AT-065.

title: The new add-a-case form silently discards a submission whose steps duplicate an existing case -- 303 redirect, no case added, no message, so a user who mistyped a title and re-submits believes it worked
evidence: Found by the checker while probing unit ui-add-case live. Case.compute_id() hashes only (project, flow_id, case_class, steps) -- title and rationale are excluded -- and ProjectStore.add_case (store/project_store.py:71-79) is idempotent on id: `if case.id in self._case_ids: return case`, appending nothing. Reproduced on a scratch project: POST /projects/xssprobe/cases with title 'A completely different title' and the same two steps as an existing case returned 303 to /projects/xssprobe, cases.jsonl stayed at 1 line, and the stored title remained the ORIGINAL one. ui/routes_cases.py::create_case does not compare add_case's returned case against what it built, so it cannot tell an insert from a no-op and shows nothing either way. Not a violation of any current ui.md criterion (U1 only requires that a created case be a real CLI-compatible Case, which it is) -- filed so the silent-discard UX gap becomes queued work rather than folklore. Related to but distinct from AT-059: the same id-excludes-title/rationale design, seen from the UI side. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): Duplicate-steps submissions are explicitly refused in src/autotester/ui/routes_cases.py rather than silently swallowed.
checker_note: Fixed by unit ui-case-management cycle 1 (verdict qa/verdicts/ui-case-management.md). Checker re-derived live against localhost:8010, not the maker's paste: re-posting the identical steps with a different title now returns HTTP 400 naming the EXISTING case's current title ("this project already has a case with exactly these steps: 'Renamed OK'. Change a step to make it a different case, or rename the existing one from the cases list.") and writes nothing, instead of a 303 that silently discarded the submission. The second half of the fix is the recovery path the issue implied but did not name: GET /projects/<slug>/cases lists every case, POST .../<case_id>/rename changes the title while keeping the content-addressed id (so rubric, RawResults and Verdicts stay attached -- verified on disk), and POST .../<case_id>/delete removes the row and nothing else (before/after tree diff: zero files removed). Residuals filed as AT-066 and AT-067.

title: _require_reachable_base_url's 'browser can open it' half is much weaker than it reads -- host_of returns a non-empty pseudo-host for arbitrary garbage, so a base_url with no scheme (or literally 'all') still onboards a project no browser can open
evidence: Found by /checker while probing unit ui-project-edit-and-domain-validation live. src/autotester/ui/helpers.py:53-55 refuses only when host_of() returns EMPTY, and browser/secrets.py:70-84 returns empty only for a backslash, userinfo, or an unparseable authority -- urlparse('//all').hostname is 'all'. Reproduced against localhost:8010: POST /onboard slug=chk-garbage base_url=all allowed_domains=all -> HTTP 303, projects/chk-garbage/project.json written with base_url 'all'; POST /onboard slug=chk-noscheme base_url=vidysea.com allowed_domains=vidysea.com -> HTTP 303, stored schemeless. Both self-consistent, so the AT-058 half of the validator correctly passes them; both would still die at page.goto. Not a FAIL of this unit: the manifest's claim is literally 'host_of returns empty' and that is exactly what the code does, and no ui.md criterion requires scheme validation. Fix direction if queued: require a http/https scheme in the UI layer (a Pydantic AnyHttpUrl-style check on base_url), NOT by tightening host_of, which is the shared credential-boundary primitive and must keep failing closed on exactly the cases it names.

title: Onboarding and the new edit form disagree on whitespace: edit strips name/base_url before saving, onboarding stores them verbatim, so the same value entered in the two places produces two different project.json files
evidence: Found by /checker while probing unit ui-project-edit-and-domain-validation live. ui/routes_project_edit.py:72-74 saves name.strip() and base_url.strip(); ui/app.py::onboard_submit passes name and base_url straight into Project(...) with no strip (only allowed_domains is split-and-stripped in both). Reproduced: POST /onboard slug=chk-ws name='  padded  ' base_url='  https://sub.example.com/x  ' -> HTTP 303 and projects/chk-ws/project.json holds '"name": "  padded  "' and '"base_url": "  https://sub.example.com/x  "' verbatim. Harmless today because host_of tolerates surrounding whitespace, so validation and navigation both still resolve the right host, and the padded name is escaped on render -- filed as a consistency gap so the divergence is queued work rather than folklore. Fix direction: strip in onboard_submit too, or better, strip once inside the shared helper both routes already call.

title: is_stale_default compares only criteria and no_fire, so a human edit confined to a rubric's feedback_format is silently discarded when the rubric is regenerated for a stale claim
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation. src/autotester/stages/run_case_pipeline.py:83 returns `rubric.criteria == untouched.criteria and rubric.no_fire == untouched.no_fire` -- Rubric.feedback_format (schema/verdict.py:36, consumed by stages/grade.py:47 as {{FORMAT}}) is not part of the comparison. Reproduced in-container: a rubric from default_rubric(old_case) with feedback_format set to 'custom human format' and a changed case rationale gives is_stale_default == True, so run_and_grade_case overwrites it and the custom format is lost. Not a FAIL of this unit: no contract criterion covers feedback_format, regeneration is the desired behaviour in that scenario (the claim really was stale), and no code path anywhere sets feedback_format -- grep finds only the schema default and grade.py's read -- so the field is reachable only by hand-editing JSON. Fix direction if queued: include feedback_format in the untouched-comparison, or document it as deliberately excluded because it is presentation, not the grading claim.

title: A generator-stamped rubric shared by two cases via case.rubric_ref would be rewritten with the pointing case's claim, destroying the other case's grading contract
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation. run_case_pipeline.py:96 resolves `rubric_id = case.rubric_ref or f'rub_{case.id}'`, and is_stale_default (line 82) rebuilds the untouched shape with `rubric.case_id or case.id` -- it never checks that rubric.case_id actually IS this case. Reproduced in-container: a rubric carrying GENERATOR provenance whose case_id is 'some_other_case_id' returns is_stale_default == True against an unrelated case, so run_and_grade_case would save that case's claim over it. Unreachable today: grep over src, scripts and tests finds rubric_ref only in its schema declaration (schema/case.py:30), its copy in Case.with_fixed_step (case.py:60) and this one read -- nothing ever assigns it, so no shared rubric can exist yet. Filed so it is queued work rather than folklore before the first rubric_ref writer lands. Fix direction: return False when rubric.case_id is set and != case.id.

title: The 4 pre-existing unstamped rubrics on disk are NOT in fact indistinguishable from hand-written ones -- they carry the generator's exact template -- but they can never self-heal, so AT-059's failure mode stays latent for those cases
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation. The manifest's stated limitation says rubrics written before provenance stamping are 'genuinely indistinguishable from hand-written ones'. Checker-verified against all 5 rubric files in the 4 real projects: projects/pathlynks/rubrics/{rub_case_35b17ccece2d,rub_case_a5ea57c0961a,rub_case_b1cb019ebb56}.json and projects/vidysea-erp/rubrics/rub_case_7ba94f4da443.json all have provenance null AND carry _rubric_for_claim's exact output -- a single criterion id 'c1' with the text "The evidence is consistent with: <claim>. If you cite this as a failure, use criterion id 'c1' exactly - do not invent a different id." and no_fire == ['exact wording of any error message shown by the product']. Every hand-written rubric in the repo differs in shape (scripts/run_pathlynks_first_cases.py:91 uses criterion id 'landed'; scripts/regression_proof.py:93 and scripts/bench_trial.py:83 use no_fire ['visual styling'] and different wording), so shape alone does distinguish them. Consequence: those 4 rubrics are permanently pinned to their embedded claim; if any of those cases' rationale is later corrected, AT-059's exact live failure recurs and hand-deleting the file is again the only recovery. Currently harmless -- checker re-derived claim_of(case) for all 5 and none is stale today, and none would be rewritten by the next run. Not a FAIL: refusing to touch an unstamped rubric is the safe direction, and a template-shape heuristic would reintroduce exactly the overwrite-on-a-guess risk the unit exists to avoid. Fix direction if queued: a one-off migration that stamps provenance on rubrics whose shape is byte-identical to _rubric_for_claim(embedded_claim, ...), reviewed by a human per file -- not an automatic runtime heuristic.

title: test_deleting_then_re_adding_the_same_steps_works cannot exercise the _case_ids cache it is documented as proving -- every UI request builds a fresh ProjectStore, so the test would pass unchanged even if delete_case never discarded the id
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-case-management. tests/test_ui_case_management.py:166-181 asserts that a delete followed by a re-add of identical steps succeeds, and both the test docstring and qa/manifests/ui-case-management.md claim this 'proves delete_case genuinely clears the id cache rather than leaving the duplicate guard to refuse a legitimate re-add'. It does not: src/autotester/ui/helpers.py:73 constructs `store = ProjectStore(slug)` per request, so ProjectStore._case_ids is None at the start of every HTTP call and is repopulated from disk by has_case/add_case. Deleting the `self._case_ids.discard(case_id)` line in project_store.py:116 would leave the test green. The checker verified the actual cache behaviour separately, in-container, within ONE store instance: add -> has_case True; delete_case -> True and has_case False; re-add of the identical (same-id) case in that same instance -> the row comes back (list_cases == ['B']); update_case keeps the id in the cache. So the CODE is correct -- only the test's proof-value claim is overstated. Not a FAIL of any ui.md criterion (none governs test coverage). Fix direction if queued: assert directly against one ProjectStore instance (add/delete/has_case/add), or drop the claim from the docstring and manifest. | FIXED 2026-09-07: added three store-level tests in tests/test_store.py that exercise the id cache against ONE ProjectStore instance, where it is actually observable: delete clears it (has_case False, and the re-add a stale cache would swallow succeeds), delete of an unknown id returns False, and update_case keeps the id cached while replacing in place rather than appending twice. Proof-value verified by sabotage, not assumed: replacing `self._case_ids.discard(case_id)` with a dead branch makes test_delete_case_clears_the_id_cache_within_one_store_instance FAIL, while the UI-level test AT-066 was filed against still passes -- which is precisely the gap the checker identified. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): Store-level id-cache tests are present in tests/test_store.py and the suite passes.

title: cases.jsonl whole-file rewrite (delete_case/update_case) can silently drop a row appended concurrently by a CLI script's add_case -- pre-existing with upsert_jsonl, now reachable from a UI button
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-case-management. store/filestore.py:75-88 (delete_jsonl_row) and :91-110 (upsert_jsonl) both read the whole file, filter/replace in memory, and _atomic_write the result -- a read-modify-write with no lock. Any row appended between the read and the os.replace is lost. Repo-wide the only writers to projects/<slug>/cases.jsonl are ProjectStore.add_case (append_jsonl), update_case and delete_case; grep over src and scripts finds add_case call sites at ui/routes_cases.py:188, scripts/bench_trial.py:118, scripts/regression_proof.py:147 and scripts/run_pathlynks_first_cases.py:161. There is no in-process concurrency (helpers.py:73 builds a fresh ProjectStore per request and nothing runs in the background), so the only real window is a human running one of those CLI scripts while clicking Rename/Delete in the UI. The write itself IS atomic -- checker-verified that a crash cannot truncate the file: mkstemp in the target's own directory, write, os.replace, unlink on any BaseException, and no orphan .tmp-* left on the success path. Both docstrings already state the caveat ('for a small collection a human curates, never for append-only history'). Not a FAIL: the unit introduces no new concurrency and no criterion covers it. Fix direction if queued: an advisory lock file per project directory around the read-modify-write, or make delete/update go through a single serialised writer.

title: The declare-secret 400 echoes the raw submitted key back to the caller -- and the form's own hint says the most likely wrong entry there is the credential VALUE itself
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-secrets-declaration. src/autotester/ui/routes_project_edit.py:176 raises `HTTPException(400, f"cannot declare '{key.strip()}': {why}")`. Reproduced live in-container: `POST /projects/erp/secrets key=hunter2` returns `{"detail":"cannot declare 'hunter2': String should match pattern '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$'"}` with content-type application/json. The card's own hint text (_secrets_card, line 75-76) reads 'CAPITALS, digits and underscores -- a name, never the value itself', which names pasting the value into the Key field as the anticipated user error; when that happens the value is reflected verbatim in the response body. NOT an XSS (the body is JSON, not HTML -- verified via content-type) and nothing is persisted (erp's secrets were unchanged after the probe), so no U3/U5 criterion is violated and this is not a FAIL. The exposure is bounded to the submitter's own response on a localhost single-operator tool, but it is the one place in this unit where a would-be credential is repeated back rather than dropped, and the project's stated discipline is that values are never echoed (routes_credentials.py never echoes the posted value). Fix direction if queued: drop the key from the message ('that is not a valid credential name: <reason>'), or echo only a length/shape summary. | FIXED 2026-09-07: the 400 no longer quotes the submitted key -- it reads 'cannot declare this credential: <pydantic msg>'. The form hint was also reworded to stop naming the value as a thing that could go in that box; it now says the box wants a NAME and that the value is entered later on the Credentials page. Regression test test_a_rejected_key_is_never_echoed_back asserts a password-shaped key is refused and its text absent from the response. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): test_a_rejected_key_is_never_echoed_back present in the test suite and passing.

title: routes_project_edit.py's module docstring cites ledger id AT-068 as this unit's tracker, but no such row existed when the code was written -- and AT-068 is now an unrelated defect
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-secrets-declaration. src/autotester/ui/routes_project_edit.py:13 reads 'This module also owns the project's `SecretRef` declarations (Track 0 / AT-068).' At the time of this check the ledger's highest id was AT-067 (verified: `grep -o '"id": "AT-[0-9]*"' qa/issues.jsonl | sort -t- -k2 -n | tail -1` -> AT-067) and qa/manifests/ui-secrets-declaration.md states 'Issues addressed: none filed yet', so AT-068 was a forward reference to a row that was never written. AT-068 has since been allocated by this same check to an unrelated finding (the 400 key echo), so the docstring pointer now resolves to a real but wrong row -- worse than a dangling one, because a reader following it lands on a defect rather than on this unit's rationale. Contrast the same file's line 3 'AT-058:' pointer, which does resolve correctly. Not a FAIL: no ui.md criterion governs comment accuracy, and doctor/ruff pass. Fix direction: cite qa/manifests/ui-secrets-declaration.md (the actual record of this work) instead of a ledger id, or file a real ledger row for the Track 0 prerequisite and cite that. | FIXED 2026-09-07: docstring now cites 'Track 0, Unit 0.1 of the 2026-09-07 plan; gate qa/gates/at052-bfs-video-corpus-grill.md' instead of a ledger id that did not exist when written. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): src/autotester/ui/routes_project_edit.py module docstring no longer cites the non-existent AT-068 tracker.

title: The paste-a-real-credential guard is applied to step_value ONLY -- the same credential typed into the case title, step_target or step_expected is accepted and written in cleartext to projects/<slug>/cases.jsonl, which IS git-tracked in a public repo
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. src/autotester/ui/routes_cases.py:116 calls `_refuse_unsafe_value(value.strip(), project, secrets)` inside _build_steps and nowhere else; `title` (routes_cases.py:154-157, checked only for non-blank), `target` (:121) and `expect` (:117-120) reach `Step`/`Case` unchecked. Reproduced in-container against a scratch AUTOTESTER_ROOT with a declared DEMO_PASSWORD whose .env value was 'hunter2-this-is-the-real-one': step_value=<value> -> 400 refused (correct); the identical value in step_target -> 303 and on disk as {"target":"hunter2-this-is-the-real-one"}; in step_expected -> 303 and on disk as {"expected":{"visible_text":["hunter2-this-is-the-real-one"]}}; in the title -> 303 and on disk as the case title. The manifest's own stated reason for the guard ('cases.jsonl is not gitignored') applies verbatim to all three: `git check-ignore .env` -> ignored by **/.env, but `git ls-files projects/pathlynks/cases.jsonl` returns the path, so that file is tracked and this repo is public (github.com/umeshsugara-ai/autoTesting). The three boxes sit on the SAME form row as the guarded one, so this is a plausible mis-field, not an attack. The title case is worse than a storage leak: `stages/run_case_pipeline.claim_of` returns `f"the case '{case.title}' completes as its steps describe"` when rationale is None (which U6 mandates), so the raw value reaches build_grade_prompt -- where the newly-wired `SecretStore.guard_prompt` then raises an UNHANDLED ValueError, turning every subsequent run into a 500 rather than a graded verdict (verified: REAL in claim_of(case) -> True; grade(..., secrets=store) on a payload carrying the value -> ValueError 'refusing to proceed: raw secret value present in payload'). Not a FAIL of any ui.md criterion -- none governs credential safety in cases; the maker correctly filed nothing and this row is the tracker. Fix direction: move the guard from _build_steps' value branch to every user-supplied string create_case persists (title, target, expected text), keeping the placeholder-vs-literal split as it is.

title: The raw-value guard is per-step-row, so a credential split across two rows passes and reassembles exactly -- the control is defence-in-depth, not a boundary, and the manifest presents it as protection
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. `Redactor.is_clean` (core/redact.py:52-54) tests `value in text` for each whole known .env value, and `_refuse_unsafe_value` is called once per surviving step row (routes_cases.py:116), so no cross-row or cross-field view of the submission exists. Reproduced in-container on a scratch root whose .env held only DEMO_PASSWORD=hunter2-this-is-the-real-one: a two-row submission with step_value[0]='hunter2-this-i' and step_value[1]='s-the-real-one' -> 303, both halves persisted to cases.jsonl, and half0+half1 == the real value byte for byte. Note this probe had to be re-run: a first attempt appeared to be caught, but only because the scratch .env also carried SHORT=a and the second half contains an 'a' -- the checker does not report a pass it cannot reproduce cleanly. Correctly CAUGHT in the same harness: the exact value; the value with surrounding whitespace (_build_steps strips before the guard, confirmed order at routes_cases.py:116); the value as a substring of a longer string ('prefix-<value>-suffix'); and an UNDECLARED .env value belonging to another project, because SecretStore.redactor() is built from _all_values() = shadow + declared (browser/secrets.py:_all_values). Severity medium not high: this needs deliberate action, unlike AT-070's adjacent-box slip. Fix direction: none required as a code change -- but the manifest/docs should say what this control is (a mistake-catcher over exact known values), so nobody later mistakes it for a boundary.

title: is_clean has no minimum length by design (AT-002), so a short or word-like .env value makes ordinary step text be refused with a message that wrongly tells the user they pasted a credential
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. core/redact.py:20-24 documents the absence of a minimum length as deliberate ('a three-character password is a bad password, but leaking it is still a leak'), and the checker agrees the direction is right -- it fails CLOSED. The cost is the message, not the refusal. Reproduced in-container with a scratch .env holding DEMO_TOKEN=test: step_value 'test' -> 400, 'latest news' -> 400, 'contest entry' -> 400, 'Bengaluru' -> 303. The refusal text is 'that looks like a real credential. Do not paste the value into a test step...', which is simply false for 'latest news' and gives the user no way to understand or proceed. This is live-reachable today, not hypothetical: the repo-root .env carries PATHLYNKS_USER_LOGIN_URL, a non-secret URL, so any step value containing that URL is now refused as 'a real credential' (that same URL already appears legitimately as a navigate target in the tracked projects/pathlynks/cases.jsonl). Not a FAIL: no ui.md criterion covers message accuracy, and refusing is the safe direction. Fix direction: name the declared key in the message when the match is a declared value ('that is the value of DEMO_TOKEN -- use {{SECRET:DEMO_TOKEN}} instead'), which is honest, actionable, and leaks nothing the user did not just type.

title: Three routes still write a raw .env value in cleartext to git-tracked project.json: POST /onboard (name), POST /projects/{slug}/edit (name) and POST /projects/{slug}/secrets (description). None calls the credential guard. The value is also echoed in the response and then rendered on EVERY page (the home index lists project names). Breaches core-invariants C5 ('secret values live only in the repo-root .env').

title: DEFAULT_NEVER_CLICK_PATTERNS misses hyphen/underscore/dot-separated logout control names -- "Log-Out", "Sign-Out", "LOG_OUT", and "Log.Out" all return None from deny_reason (not denied), because both never-click patterns use [\s\w]{0,10} or a literal " ?" between the two words, and neither \s nor \w matches a hyphen, underscore, or dot. This is a coverage gap in the never-click baseline itself (schema/crawl.py DEFAULT_NEVER_CLICK_PATTERNS), not a policy-construction bypass -- AT-092's fix (checking the baseline unconditionally) is unaffected and still correctly denies every space/adjacent-word variant it targets. title: store/filestore.py::append_jsonl documents itself as "cheap and crash-safe (a torn write can only ever damage the last line, never an earlier one)", but read_jsonl RAISES ValueError on any malformed row rather than skipping it -- so a torn final line does not merely damage that line, it makes the ENTIRE file unloadable. This narrows the explore.md X11 partial-graph guarantee more than the docstring implies: a crawl killed BETWEEN writes leaves a fully loadable graph (checker proved this live), but a crawl killed DURING a single node/edge/issue append leaves nodes.jsonl unreadable and the partial graph lost. Affects every JSONL artifact in the system (cases, results, issues), not just crawls -- the crawl stage is simply the first writer that runs long enough for a mid-append kill to be realistic. Not a defect introduced by this unit; the honest scope is now recorded in qa/contracts/explore.md X11. Fix options: have read_jsonl tolerate a malformed FINAL line (skip with a warning) while still raising on a malformed interior line, or write each row with a single atomic os.write of a pre-encoded buffer.
evidence: src/autotester/store/filestore.py:67-72 append_jsonl (docstring claims crash-safe) vs :52-64 read_jsonl ("A malformed row raises with its line number" -- raises ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: {exc}")). Checker proof of the covered case, run inside docker compose exec autotester: monkeypatched explore_node.visit_node to raise KeyboardInterrupt on the 2nd node -> partial graph loaded OK, 3 nodes, 3 edges, statuses ['explored','queued'], envelope status=running finished_at=None. The mid-append case was NOT induced and is not claimed to be safe.

title: stages/explore.py::_seed swallows the seed exception entirely (except Exception: return None), so a crawl that cannot start reports the single generic stop_reason "could not open base_url" with the cause discarded -- a NavigationRefused (the X7 security refusal) is indistinguishable from a DNS failure, a timeout or a TLS error.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore.py:93-98 `_seed`: try { goto(base_url); settle(); observe() } except Exception: return None -- the exception object is never bound, logged, or attached to the crawl. Caller at :179-181: `if _seed(rt) is None: rt.stop_reason = "could not open base_url"; return _finish(rt, CrawlStatus.ABORTED)`. Detection is NOT lost (the crawl does abort and does say so), but the diagnosis is: every distinct failure mode collapses to one string. This bites T-145 directly (the live logged-in ERP crawl), where an operator seeing "could not open base_url" cannot tell whether the ERP was down or whether the crawl was refused by its own domain guard. Related and lower: `_recover` at explore_node.py:145-150 is `except Exception: pass`, so a failed recovery is unrecorded -- though the caller returns False regardless, so the node status is still written. Fix direction: bind the exception and set stop_reason to f"could not open base_url: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", and record NavigationRefused distinctly from a transport error. Not a contract-sanctioned fallback: qa/contracts/explore.md does not ask for the cause to be dropped -- contrast explore_node.capture, whose "never fatal" swallow IS documented B7 behaviour and is deliberately NOT flagged here.

title: explore_merge.merge_screens raises a Conflict only when the clashing names DIFFER, so a screen re-discovered at a known url_pattern under the SAME name is added as a silent duplicate -- the FlowSpec ends up with two identically-named screens on one pattern and no Conflict row telling the human why.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_merge.py:105 `if clash is not None and clash.name != incoming.name:`. Probed live 2026-09-08 (checker-authored script, container /tmp): spec seeded with Screen(id='scr_old', name='Students', url_pattern='/students/{id}'), merged one crawled node whose name is also 'Students' -> screens 2, conflicts 0, both rows ('scr_old','Students','/students/{id}') and ('node_f8417a9609e9','Students','/students/{id}'). X13 is not violated (the existing screen is preserved, review resets to DRAFT), and X14 as authored scopes itself to 'under a different name' -- so this is a residual, not a criterion violation. Fix direction: key the conflict on identity (a different Screen.id on an already-claimed pattern) rather than on the name string, or dedupe-by-signature so a same-name re-discovery merges instead of duplicating.

title: The (correct) same-crawl SPA exemption in merge_screens is scoped to ONE CRAWL, not to one SOURCE: a second SPA state discovered by a LATER crawl at a url_pattern an earlier crawl already merged does file a Conflict, even though both claims come from the crawler and neither disagrees with the other.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_merge.py:99-100 `by_pattern = {s.url_pattern: s for s in spec.screens if s.url_pattern}` is built from the PRE-EXISTING spec only, and screens added during this merge are put into `known_ids` but never into `by_pattern` -- which is exactly what makes the intra-crawl exemption work. Probed live 2026-09-08: the identical SPA pair (same '/' pattern, signatures sig_plain / sig_filters, names 'Home' and 'Home with filters open') gives screens=2 conflicts=0 when merged in one call, and screens=2 conflicts=1 when merged as crawl c1 then crawl c2 -- claims ["existing screen 'Home' (node_4c6a215b75e5)", "crawled screen 'Home with filters open' (node_16734fb626aa)"]. Consequence: a project that re-crawls (the intended workflow -- the UI has an 'Explore again' button) accumulates false Conflicts on every SPA whose states are found across separate crawls. Fails safe (both screens are kept, nothing is overwritten), so it is noise for the human reviewer rather than data loss. Fix direction: exempt a clash whose existing screen's source_ref.source_id is itself a crawl id, i.e. scope the exemption to 'the crawler as a source' rather than 'this crawl run'.

title: explore_node.return_to() discards the cause of a failed return -- the same shape AT-098 just fixed at _seed, one level down. A NavigationRefused (the X7 SECURITY refusal) hit while getting back onto a node is indistinguishable from a timeout or a torn page, and the first call site records no reason at all.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_node.py:135-138 `except Exception: _recover(rt); return False` -- the exception is never bound. Two call sites in visit_node: :182 `if not return_to(...): _mark(rt, node, NodeStatus.ABORTED_ERROR); return` records the node status with NO reason string anywhere, and :198 records an edge with the fixed literal 'could not return to this screen'. So a crawl that stops exploring a node because the browser was refused off-domain on the way back reads exactly like one that hit a slow page. AT-098's own evidence flagged this as 'related and lower' (_recover at explore_node.py:145-150 is `except Exception: pass`); AT-098 is closed on its stated scope (_seed), so the residual is filed here rather than lost. Not a criterion violation: no X-criterion requires a return_to reason, and it fails safe -- the node is marked and the crawl continues. Fix direction: bind the exception in return_to, return the reason, and pass it into _mark / record_edge the way try_action already does at :103-107. Deliberately NOT flagged: explore_node.py:33 (capture's 'never fatal' swallow, documented B7 behaviour) and _recover's own inner `except Exception: pass` (last-ditch recovery, the caller already returns False).
checker_note: Fixed by 6e98487 (unit at108-at114-swallowed-causes), checker-verified cycle 1: all four sabotages independently reproduced in a git-archive scratch copy.

title: The AT-103 fix widened the SPA exemption from 'one crawl' to 'both claims are structural', which also makes a GENUINE product change unreportable: a later crawl finding a structurally different screen at a url_pattern an earlier crawl already claimed is now silently two screens and never a Conflict, and the stale screen is kept forever with nothing marking it stale.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_merge.py:110 `if clash is None or clash.name == incoming.name or _is_structural(clash): return None`. Probed live 2026-09-08 (checker script, container): crawl c1 finds /settings (sig_v1, 'Settings'); the product ships a redesign; crawl c2 finds /settings (sig_v2, 'Account settings') and v1 no longer exists -> screens=2 conflicts=0, both rows kept ('node_1adc40552' src=c1, 'node_bc8e052c9' src=c2), review note '1 screen(s) added by crawl c2 -- needs review' -- byte-identical to what an innocent SPA re-crawl says, so the human cannot tell the two apart. Two crawls at different times ARE two sources with distinct source_ids and their claims genuinely differ; pre-fix (a195fbf) this filed a Conflict. NOT a violation of X14 as written (its own AT-103 residual paragraph prescribed this widening) and it fails safe -- both screens survive, nothing is overwritten, the version bumps and Review resets to DRAFT -- so it is a residual, not a regression to revert. Note also that a Conflict was always a poor instrument here: it caught a product change only when the URL was kept AND the name changed, and never caught a screen that vanished or moved. Fix direction: do NOT re-narrow _is_structural (that reinstates a false conflict on every SPA state on every re-crawl, which is the intended workflow -- the UI has an 'Explore again' button). Add the missing mechanism instead: last-seen/staleness on Screen (a screen not observed by the latest crawl of this project), surfaced on the crawl page and the workbook, which reports disappearance and redesign alike.

title: The RunApproval tamper check is defeated by recomputing the id: content_id is an UNKEYED sha256, so anyone who can write approvals.jsonl -- including the autonomous crawler the gate exists to bound -- can widen a grant and mint a matching id. Caught a careless edit, did not stop a forger.
evidence: Proven end to end on disk in the running container, scratch AUTOTESTER_ROOT=/tmp/advroot2. Baseline: a human grant of max_actions=12 via `uv run autotester approve` -> appr_f3616d0cafd7. (a) Editing max_actions to 9999 while keeping the stored id IS caught: `check_crawl_approval.py demo` and a real `autotester explore` both refuse with 'appr_f3616d0cafd7: edited after it was granted (content id no longer matches)'. (b) Rewriting the same row with max_actions=9999, wall_clock_s=99999.0, production=True and the `id` key REMOVED -> schema/approval.py model_post_init mints the matching id (id has default ""), forged row appr_34d709b1d3ea, is_intact=True. Pasting a self-computed id is identical. `AUTOTESTER_ROOT=/tmp/advroot2 uv run autotester explore demo --max-actions 500 --wall-clock 300` then RAN: crawl_01M1ZD9VR9SKRN9B748KKH721V completed -- a 500-action production-flagged crawl on a human grant of 12. Root cause: core/ids.py content_id() is a plain sha256 with no secret, so the mapping is public. NOT charged as a failure -- CN3 as filed claims only id-mismatch detection, which is exactly true, and no unkeyed local scheme can do better. HUMAN_GATE for Umesh (do not let the maker pick): HMAC keyed from the repo-root .env (already the credential boundary and gitignored), a separate signed/append-only audit line, or is 'accident detection only' the accepted posture? Independently of that decision, the operator-facing prose overclaims and must be corrected: schema/approval.py module docstring ('an approval cannot be edited on disk to widen itself') and cli_crawl.approve_cmd's docstring, which is `--help` text an operator reads ('editing the row afterwards to widen it invalidates it'). Recorded as a stated limitation in qa/contracts/consent.md CN3.
checker_note: PROSE HALF CLOSED by cycle 2 (1d2e647); the design half stays open and is a HUMAN_GATE (qa/gates/at110-approval-forgery.md). Checker cycle 2 re-read both operator surfaces: schema/approval.py's module docstring now states 'Do not read the check below as tamper *proofing*; it is tamper *evidence*' and names the 9999/production forgery, and `uv run autotester approve --help` renders 'this is tamper EVIDENCE, not tamper proofing: anyone who can write approvals.jsonl can recompute a valid id (AT-110)'. grep for 'cannot be edited'/'tamper-proof' over src/ and scripts/ returns nothing. Behaviour re-run and UNCHANGED, as required -- only the claim changed: on a real 12-action grant (appr_77d1ba6115a2), editing max_actions to 9999 with the id kept is still refused ('edited after it was granted'), and dropping the `id` key while widening to max_actions=9999/wall_clock_s=99999/production=true is still ACCEPTED and still runs (crawl_01M1ZN1Q68PE8WKVJNQ7YMNMMB completed on a human grant of 12). title: CN1 fails at both shipped entry points: a REFUSED crawl still creates projects/<slug>/crawl/<crawl_id>/shots/ and launches Chromium, because BrowserSession.start() runs inside the `with` that wraps run_crawl. The 'leaves no trace' invariant is proven only on the direct run_crawl call that no operator uses.
evidence: Measured live in the container against fb261c5. CLI: `AUTOTESTER_ROOT=/tmp/advroot uv run autotester explore demo --max-actions 12 --wall-clock 30` printed the correct refusal and exited 2, and left /tmp/advroot/projects/demo/crawl/crawl_01M1ZD6SPNYWVANSFV8EK4BBZN/shots/ plus a fully populated Chromium profile under /tmp/advroot/profiles/demo/ (Cookies, History, Preferences, Local State, LOG) -- i.e. a real browser was launched for a run that was then refused. Chain: cli_crawl.py explore_cmd and ui/routes_crawls.py start_crawl both compute paths.crawl_shots_dir(crawl_id) and enter `with BrowserSession(...)` BEFORE calling run_crawl; browser/session.py:103 start() does self.state.run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True). stages/explore.py _require_consent then fires from inside that context. No outward-facing action occurs (goto is inside run_crawl, so the target is never contacted) -- this is a trace/hygiene and truth-in-claims failure, not an exposure. Fix direction: call the consent check before `with BrowserSession(...)` in both callers (make stages/explore._require_consent public; the seam check STAYS -- qa/contracts/consent.md CN2 explicitly permits a caller-side pre-check in addition to the seam), which also stops the pointless browser launch; alternatively make session.start()'s run_dir.mkdir lazy, which fixes the directory but not the launch. That propagation dies one frame up. Also outside session.py's own try: page.add_style_tag(MASK_CSS) at :259 -- if the B7 mask fails to apply, capture() swallows it too (no unmasked leak, since no shot is then taken, but the operator is never told the crawl has screens it could not photograph). T-145 -- the live production-ERP crawl -- was raised to CRITICAL this cycle and still classifies 'low', so it will get a SINGLE checker instead of the dual check the escalation was meant to buy.

D:/ai_os/.claude/skills/goal/scripts/criticality.py:11 _ORDER = {"low": 0, "medium": 1, "high": 2, "critical": 3}; base_criticality() at :40 is `b = task.get("base_criticality"); return b if b in _ORDER else "low"`. title: The `autotester crawl` CLI one-liner -- the surface a headless or CI run actually reads -- reports the product's issue count and omits tool_failures entirely, so the unit's own 'counted apart and REPORTED, never dropped' principle holds on the crawl page and in the workbook but not on the command line.

title: `cli_crawl.echo_crawl_summary` is the only crawl-count surface that does not guard `stop_reason`, printing the literal Python `None` where every other surface renders the `â€”` unknown sentinel.

title: A crawl artifact written before `tool_failures` existed deserialises to the Pydantic default 0 and is now displayed as a confident measured `0`, so 'the crawler recorded everything' and 'this crawl predates the counter' are again indistinguishable -- the AT-121 ambiguity with its sign flipped.

title: `VisionOptions` is honoured only when a caller passes it, and NO shipped caller does -- `autotester ingest run` delivers `options=None`, so the HIGH media resolution the schema declares for a vision call is never applied in production.

In gemini.py::_config the seed and max_output_tokens survive that (`opts = options or VisionOptions()`, verified: with options=None the config still carries seed=7, max_output_tokens=65536 -- the determinism claim the observation cache rests on HOLDS), but `media_resolution`, `temperature` and `system_instruction` all sit behind `if options is not None:` at gemini.py:73, so through the CLI media_resolution is never set at all. checker_note: fix verified by the checker at c4c878a on cycle 1 of at125-at132-declared-but-unapplied: the shipped CLI was driven directly and the sabotage reproduced in a git-archive scratch copy. Not `verified` -- that takes a later re-check.

title: `GeminiProvider._config`'s docstring says 3.x models take "`media_resolution` and a thinking level", but `thinking_level` is never put into the config -- a documented behaviour that does not exist.

title: The 3.x model test is a bare string prefix, so the SDK's fully-qualified `models/gemini-3.x` form fails it and silently loses `media_resolution` -- a wrong answer with nothing failing, the exact class this unit was built to close.

Configs built by the checker at 1c8c8e4: gemini-3.6-flash -> MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH; gemini-3-pro -> HIGH; gemini-3n-e4b -> HIGH; gemini-2.5-flash -> None (correct, falls to temperature); **models/gemini-3.6-flash -> None** (wrong -- `models/<name>` is an accepted model identifier for the google-genai SDK, and `--model` on `autotester ingest run` passes whatever string a user types straight through to GeminiProvider). title: The Files-API upload cache is keyed on `resolve()::st_size`, so a recording edited or re-exported in place at the same byte size is a cache HIT and the pipeline reads the OLD video while reporting the new one -- and this unit already computes a sha256 of the same file two modules away.
evidence: gemini_files.py:61 `key = f"{path.resolve()}::{path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else 0}"`. Reproduced by the checker at 1c8c8e4 with a stub client: upload v.mp4 (100 bytes) -> cached; rewrite the SAME path with 100 DIFFERENT bytes; call `upload_and_wait` again -> `files.upload` call count 0, the cached handle for the old content is returned. Neither content nor mtime is in the key. Every other cache-degradation path probed is CORRECT and is now required by contract I9 -- a dead handle raises inside the try and re-uploads (upload count 1), a cached handle still PROCESSING re-uploads, an expired entry (TTL 46h) misses, and a corrupt cache file (`{not json`) is swallowed by _load_cache's ValueError branch and rewritten cleanly -- so this is the one key that fails toward a plausible wrong answer instead of toward a re-upload. Probability is low (an edit landing on an identical byte count) but the consequence is a FlowSpec provenance-stamped to a recording the model never watched. Fix direction: key on `file_sha256(path)` -- `core.ids.file_sha256` is already imported by stages/ingest.py for `register_source`, so the digest for this exact file is computed anyway -- or at minimum add `st_mtime_ns`.
checker_note: fix verified by the checker at c4c878a on cycle 1 of at125-at132-declared-but-unapplied: the shipped CLI was driven directly and the sabotage reproduced in a git-archive scratch copy. Not `verified` -- that takes a later re-check.

title: `Source.sha256` is recorded at registration and never re-checked at ingest time, so `ingest_video` will watch a file whose bytes no longer match the Source describing it and stamp every SourceRef with the wrong recording's identity.
evidence: Executed by the checker at 1c8c8e4: `register_source(store, c)` with content b'v1' mints src_A carrying sha256(v1); rewriting c.mp4 to b'v2-different' and calling `register_source` again correctly mints a NEW src_B -- provenance rows are immutable, which is the right call -- but the OLD row src_A survives on disk still pointing at c.mp4 with a sha that no longer describes it. `ingest_video` (stages/ingest.py:129-145) opens `Path(source.path)` and never compares `file_sha256(path)` against `source.sha256`; `cli_video.run_cmd` selects a source by id and does not either. So `autotester ingest run demo src_A` silently watches v2 and writes a FlowSpec whose every Screen and Step SourceRef points into a video that no longer exists at those timestamps -- and I2's whole promise (a human can jump to the second the system learned a step) quietly stops being true. Nothing warns. Fix direction: verify the digest in `ingest_video` (or in `run_cmd`) and raise naming both hashes; a stale Source should be re-registered, not silently re-watched.
checker_note: fix verified by the checker at c4c878a on cycle 1 of at125-at132-declared-but-unapplied: the shipped CLI was driven directly and the sabotage reproduced in a git-archive scratch copy. Not `verified` -- that takes a later re-check.

title: `google-genai` is imported directly by `providers/gemini.py` and `gemini_files.py` but is not declared in `pyproject.toml` (plan section 4 A2 assigns the declaration to T-131); it resolves today only as a transitive dependency of `langchain-google-genai`.

But uv.lock shows exactly one package requiring it -- langchain-google-genai 4.4.0 lists `{ name = "google-genai" }` -- so GeminiProvider is importable by the accident of another library's pin, and a langchain-google-genai release that drops or renames that dependency breaks the vision provider with no pyproject change and no failing test (no test imports google.genai; the 29 tests in test_providers.py + test_ingest.py + test_ingest_persist.py all pass with socket.connect and socket.getaddrinfo blocked). title: AT-101's live-tree ban covers `git stash`/`git checkout` against COMMITTED work but says nothing about uncommitted files; the T-131 maker restored a sabotage with `git checkout` on an uncommitted prompt and destroyed its own in-progress rewrite. Self-reported by the maker and upheld here as an extension of AT-101, not as a contract criterion.
evidence: Reported in `qa/manifests/t131-ingest-persists.md` ('An accident I caused and am reporting rather than hiding'): restoring sabotage C, `git checkout src/autotester/prompts/ingest_video_v1.md` reverted the whole uncommitted rewrite, caught because `grep -c NARRATION` returned 0, then retyped. Checker verified independently that nothing was in fact lost: `git diff 1c8c8e4^ 1c8c8e4 -- src/autotester/prompts/ingest_video_v1.md` is a coherent 29-line addition carrying the complete 'What the person said' section (ground truth, align not re-transcribe, do not paraphrase, the fabricated-quote rationale), the url/fields/screenshot_ts rules and the open_questions rule; `grep -c '{{NARRATION}}'` = 1 and the three sabotage-C tests pass -- this is a full rewrite, not a degraded retype. Ruling on the maker's proposal to put a hygiene line in `qa/contracts/ingest.md`: refused in that location -- a feature contract judges the artifact, not how the maker held the tools -- and upheld here, where AT-101 already lives. title: `load_sidecar`'s `except (OSError, ValueError)` does not cover the malformed shapes its own docstring promises to survive, so a bad `<video>.transcript.json` crashes `autotester ingest run` with an unhandled traceback.
evidence: stages/ingest.py:130-131 catches only (OSError, ValueError). schema/media.py:44 `raw.get("segments", [])` raises AttributeError when the sidecar's top-level JSON is not an object; media.py:45 `TranscriptSegment(**seg)` raises TypeError when `segments` holds non-mappings. Neither is an OSError or a ValueError. Reproduced by the checker end-to-end through CliRunner on the real `app` at c4c878a: sidecar `[1,2,3]` -> `ingest run` exit=1, AttributeError; sidecar `{"segments":["hi"]}` -> exit=1, TypeError. The docstring three lines above the except reads "a malformed sidecar must not stop an ingest, because a reading with no narration is still worth having" -- a guarantee declared, plumbed, and not applied by the path that ships, which is the exact defect shape this unit exists to close. Latent on the current corpus: all 10 real *.transcript.json files are `{segments:[{start,end,text}], speech_seconds}`. Fix direction: catch the parse broadly (or validate the decoded top-level shape before touching it) so the fallback is genuinely best-effort; closing AT-134 at the same time makes the degradation audible.

title: A sidecar the loader rejects degrades silently to the prompt asserting "no speech detected" on a recording that HAS speech -- a confident false claim about ground-truth evidence, with nothing logged.
evidence: Executed by the checker through the real CLI at c4c878a: a sidecar `{"segments":[{"start":0,"end":2,"text":"real speech","confidence":0.9}]}` (one extra key; TranscriptSegment is extra="forbid") -> `ingest run` exit=0 and the rendered prompt contains "no speech detected". Nothing anywhere records that a sidecar was present and unreadable. Contract I8 requires the prompt to say no-speech WHEN NO SPEECH EXISTS; here it says it when speech exists. The maker's own AT-108/AT-114 sweep ruled that swallowing a cause is a defect, and that ruling applies to its own code. The reusable distinction: swallowing is acceptable when the fallback is NEUTRAL (a re-upload, an empty optional) and a defect when the fallback is an ASSERTION the reader will believe. Fix direction: keep the best-effort load, but emit one line on stderr naming the sidecar and the parse error; a future transcriber adding a `confidence` field must not silently blank the tester's own words.

title: Untyped refusals in the two new byte-identity paths: `verify_source_bytes` raises a raw PermissionError when the registered path is now a directory, and the AT-128 content cache key raises a bare FileNotFoundError from `upload_and_wait` where the old size key fell through to the SDK-wrapping try.
evidence: Probed by the checker at c4c878a. (1) A Source whose `path` now names a directory: `verify_source_bytes` passes `path.exists()` (true for a directory) and `file_sha256` then raises `PermissionError: [Errno 13]` on Windows -- an untyped traceback out of the CLI instead of the typed SourceChanged the function exists to produce. (2) `upload_and_wait(client, Path('does-not-exist.mp4'))` now raises FileNotFoundError from `_cache_key` -> `file_sha256` before any cache or SDK logic; the previous key (`path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else 0`) tolerated the missing file and let the SDK call raise inside the try that re-raises as ProviderError with its cause chained (I9). Neither is a live failure today and neither is a literal I9 violation (a missing local file is not an SDK exception), but both move a failure out of the typed-error path the contract is built around. Fix direction: `verify_source_bytes` should treat a non-file path as SourceChanged; `upload_and_wait` should let a missing local path surface as a ProviderError like every other failure it can raise.

title: The declared-but-unapplied shape survives this unit in three more places: `Source.duration_s` and `Source.notes` are written by nothing and read by nothing, and `FlowSpec.app_overview` is written and read by nothing.

title: `RepoDocs.prompts_dir` now selects between two different prompt directories on a hidden `_root_given` boolean, so `RepoDocs()` and `RepoDocs(repo_root())` are no longer equivalent constructions -- the AT-132 fix is right in effect but the seam is inferred rather than named.

title: The maker's own recurring blind spot survives on the highest-stakes surface: NO test drives the shipped `autotester explore` or `autotester approve` commands. title: The AT-147 refusal says the operator needs "tomorrow's date" but never prints it, so the one thing the operator must type is the one thing the message withholds.

title: `is_capable_of_failing` accepts `uv run pytest tests/` (and `pytest tests`, `pytest -q tests/`) -- the FULL suite, which is exactly the repo-wide shape the predicate exists to reject, and which contradicts the predicate's own docstring.

title: `is_capable_of_failing` fails OPEN by construction: it rejects a denylist of five known shapes and accepts everything else, so trivially unfailable commands sail through. Answering the maker's question: it CAN be made to fail closed, via an allowlist of task-specific forms plus an explicit written waiver.
evidence: Checker probe at b0b3eb3, predicate driven over 17 candidate commands. Accepted (False negatives, all unfailable or repo-wide): 'echo done'; 'uv run python -c "pass"'; 'test -f README.md'; 'uv run pytest --collect-only tests/test_x.py' (measured exit 0, collects without running); 'ls src/autotester/stages/merge_flowspec.py || true'; 'cat qa/contracts/ai-target.md > /dev/null || exit 0'; 'true # tests/test_x.py'; and the pytest-directory family filed separately as AT-154. Structural cause 1: the segment splitter is `command.replace('&&',';').split(';')` -- it does not split on `||`, so a `|| true` or `|| exit 0` suffix is invisible and any command can be neutered by appending one. Structural cause 2: `_is_repo_wide` returns False for every command it does not recognise, and `is_capable_of_failing` is `any(not repo_wide)`, so an unrecognised segment is scored as PROOF of task-specificity. Not filed as a FAIL of at141-at115: the manifest declares the heuristic and asks for exactly this list. Concrete fail-closed design (the better unit the maker asked for): invert to an ALLOWLIST evaluated per segment -- a segment is accepted only if it is (a) `check_deliverable.py` with at least one --exists/--contains, (b) pytest naming a part ending `.py` or containing `::` and NOT carrying --collect-only, or (c) `python scripts/<name>.py` with at least one argument; reject any command containing `||`; and give a task an escape hatch of `done_check.waiver: "<why a repo-wide command is right here>"`, which the test asserts is non-empty. Unknown shape is then rejected rather than accepted, and the hole becomes a greppable written decision instead of a silent pass.

title: The allowlist still admits four families of unconditionally-passing commands, because `_is_task_specific` matches tokens ANYWHERE in the command instead of at the program position, and disqualifies `||` but not a pipe.
evidence: Checker probe at ca18643 driving tests/test_goal_done_checks.py:is_capable_of_failing directly. Accepted (all exit 0 unconditionally): (1) `uv run pytest --co tests/x.py` -> True -- `--co` is pytest's documented short alias for `--collect-only`, which the code explicitly excludes one line away; this is the AT-154 shape recurring (the guard's own stated logic, defeated by a synonym). (2) `echo pytest tests/x.py` -> True and `uv run pytest tests/x.py | true` -> True and `uv run pytest tests/x.py |& true` -> True -- the segment splitter handles `&&`, `;` and `||` but not `|`, so a pipe neuters the exit status exactly as `|| true` did in AT-155. (3) `echo x #check_deliverable.py` -> True and `true # pytest tests/x.py` -> True -- shlex.split keeps the `#` comment tokens, so a trailing comment mentioning a recognised program is accepted; note the suite already pins `'true # tests/test_x.py'` as a must-REJECT, and adding the word `pytest` to that same comment defeats it. Root cause is one line, not three: the branch guards are `'pytest' in parts` / `'python' in parts` / `any(p.endswith('check_deliverable.py') for p in parts)` -- membership over ALL tokens, so any token anywhere (an echo argument, a comment, a pipe's right side) satisfies them. Fix direction: resolve the program token first (skip `uv`, `run`, and `-`-prefixed words, then take the first bare word) and match on THAT; split segments on `|` as well as `||`, `&&`, `;`; add `--co` to the collect-only exclusion. Not filed as a FAIL of at154-at157-fail-closed: the unit's claim is that the predicate now fails closed by default, which it verifiably does (five sabotages reproduced), and no task on disk carries any of these shapes.

title: Two of the shapes the allowlist rejects are recognition bugs in forms it already intends to accept -- `python3 scripts/x.py` and a .py under any directory other than `scripts/` -- so they would consume a waiver for no reason.

Rejected: `python3 scripts/x.py` -> False (the branch tests `'python' in parts or p.endswith('python')`, and 'python3' satisfies neither), `uv run python src/autotester/tools/x.py` -> False (the branch additionally requires the literal substring 'scripts' in the path). Everything else measured as rejected is, in the checker's ruling, correctly rejected and correctly waiver-gated: `./scripts/x.py`, `bash|sh scripts/x.sh`, `node tools/x.mjs`, `powershell -File x.ps1`, `make verify-t150`, `uv run pytest -m t150`, `uv run autotester ledger check`, `uv run python -m autotester.cli check`, `test -f <path>`, `grep -q <needle> <file>`. Fix direction: match the interpreter with a regex (`python`, `python3`, `py`) and drop the hard-coded 'scripts' path requirement, keeping the `-c` exclusion.

title: `test_a_waived_task_is_exempt_from_the_unfailable_check` does not detect deletion of the exemption it is named after: removing `and not waiver_of(t)` from the offenders comprehension leaves the whole file green.

` matched exactly once, file on disk changed, `pytest tests/test_goal_done_checks.py` -> rc 0, zero failures. title: The `|| true` neutering family still reaches through `;` and `&&`: `is_capable_of_failing` scores segments with any(), so a task-specific segment followed by an always-true segment is accepted even though the shell returns the LAST segment's exit code.
evidence: Checker probe at 62c3e65 driving tests/test_goal_done_checks.py:is_capable_of_failing directly. Accepted, all exiting 0 unconditionally: 'uv run pytest tests/x.py; true' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py && true' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py; :' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py; exit 0' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py && exit 0' -> True. Cause: is_capable_of_failing (line 115) normalises '&&' to ';', splits, and returns any(_is_task_specific(seg)) -- ALWAYS_TRUE is consulted only for the segment being scored, never for its siblings, so a no-op segment appended after a real one is invisible. Same family as AT-158's '| true' and AT-155's '|| true', reached through the two separators the splitter itself creates. Fix direction: reject the whole command when ANY segment is in ALWAYS_TRUE. Do NOT switch any() to 'the last segment must be task-specific' -- that would reject the legitimate on-disk shape 'check_deliverable.py --exists X && uv run autotester doctor' (T-126, T-150). No live instance: ';' appears in no done_check.cmd in .goal/goal.json and all six '&&' commands pair two real segments. Not filed as a FAIL of at158-at160-program-position: the unit's claims (program-position matching, the five sabotages, Z6 green at parent) all verifiably hold, and the checker ruled this should be QUEUED rather than fixed now.

title: `extract_frames` reuses any file sitting at the expected name, so a 0-byte or truncated PNG left by an interrupted run is returned as evidence and counted as a written frame.
evidence: stages/media_prep.py:102 `if png.exists() or frame_mod.extract_frame(...)`. Executed by the checker (.work/chk132/degrade.py D5): pre-creating a 0-byte `00001500.png` in the source's frames dir makes extract_frames return that path with no ffmpeg call at all -- returned frame size 0 bytes. media/frames.py:38-45 returns False on OSError/SubprocessError but does NOT unlink a partially written out_png, so a FRAME_TIMEOUT_S timeout or a Ctrl-C mid-write leaves exactly such a file and it is then cached forever. A5's rule ('references a PNG only when it exists') is satisfied by a file that exists and is not an image, and that image is shown to a human beside an issue. Breaks I-VL4. Fix direction: gate the cache on a positive size (or a decodable header) and unlink out_png in extract_frame's failure path before returning False. | CHECKER CYCLE 2: PARTIALLY fixed, STAYS OPEN. The 0-byte half is closed (media_prep.py:127 now gates the cache on st_size > 0; sabotage AI -> 1 failure, was INCONCLUSIVE) and a good cached frame is still reused without re-extracting (verified). The TRUNCATED half named in this issue and in contract invariant I-VL4 ('an empty or truncated PNG ... must not be reused') is untouched: executed by the checker -- a real 277206-byte PNG truncated to 92402 bytes at the expected name is returned by extract_frames as evidence with zero re-extract calls, and ffprobe rejects it ('chunk too big'). st_size > 0 is not a sufficient oracle. The second half of the original fix direction -- unlink out_png in extract_frame's failure path -- is also still absent (frames.py:41-42 returns False leaving the partial file), which is exactly what a FRAME_TIMEOUT_S kill leaves behind and what the cache then keeps forever. | CHECKER CYCLE 3: FIXED and VERIFIED by execution. Re-ran the cycle-2 probe: a real 276,937-byte frame truncated to 92,402 bytes at the expected name is now rejected -- extract_frames made exactly 1 extract call and the final file is 276,937 bytes with is_complete_png=True. A whole PNG at the expected name is still reused with 0 extract calls. A killed extract (FRAME_TIMEOUT_S forced to 0.05s) returned False and left NO file behind; an OSError from a missing ffmpeg likewise. is_complete_png attacked with 8 shapes: truncated=False, trailing-garbage-appended=False, wrong-magic-right-tail=False, 0-byte=False, a DIRECTORY at the path=False (OSError caught), whole PNG=True. Residual, filed as its own low finding rather than charged here: a 20-byte file that is exactly PNG magic + IEND returns True -- not reachable from a killed write, which truncates the tail.

title: `plan_chunks` refuses an overlap >= chunk but not a NEGATIVE overlap, which silently produces uncovered gaps; an infinite duration OOMs and a NaN duration silently plans nothing.
evidence: Executed by the checker (.work/chk132/attack.py): plan_chunks(500.0, overlap_s=-30.0) -> [(0.0,180.0),(210.0,180.0),(420.0,80.0)] -- the interval [180,210) is covered by no chunk and nothing reports it. chunks.py:48 guards only `overlap_s >= chunk_s`. Also plan_chunks(inf) -> MemoryError (unbounded list build; probe.py:58 does float() on ffprobe's duration string and float('inf') parses); plan_chunks(nan) -> [] silently. The no-gap property is otherwise sound: 2000 randomised (duration, chunk, overlap>=0) triples produced 0 gapless failures, and duration==chunk_s, chunk_s+1, overlap 0, and 1e9/1e6 all behave; the 0.1-accumulation case (chunk 0.3 / overlap 0.1 over 1000s, 4999 chunks) stays gapless. Fix direction: reject overlap_s < 0 and a non-finite duration in the guard that already rejects overlap >= chunk. | CHECKER CYCLE 2: FIXED. Re-executed: plan_chunks(500,overlap_s=-30) -> ValueError 'cannot be negative'; plan_chunks(inf) and plan_chunks(nan) -> ValueError 'duration must be finite'; chunk_s 0/-10/inf -> ValueError 'positive, finite'. Sabotage AJ -> 1 (was INCONCLUSIVE).

title: The `-ss`-after-`-i` rationale asserted in three docstrings and in the manifest is falsified on the ffmpeg actually in use -- input-side seeking measured accurate, so the stated cost buys a benefit that was not measured.
evidence: chunks.py:77-83, frames.py:28-35 and the t132 manifest all state that `-ss` before `-i` seeks to the nearest keyframe and can land seconds away. Executed by the checker on ffmpeg 8.1.1 with the real corpus: `ffmpeg -y -i erp1.mp4 -ss 20 -frames:v 1` and `ffmpeg -y -ss 20 -i erp1.mp4 -frames:v 1` produced BYTE-IDENTICAL PNGs (md5 670362ad938c57b42431d432ce4d9abb) despite keyframes at 4.27s intervals (17.07 and 21.33 bracket t=20). The PLACEMENT property itself is real and was verified independently: chunk_01_9s.mp4's first frame peaks against the original at exactly t=9.0 (PSNR 43.63, vs 37.58 at the 8.53 keyframe and 35.45 at 9.5). Both surviving -ss docstrings (chunks.py:93-103, frames.py:28-38) now state the original justification was wrong and cite the checker's byte-identical measurement; grep for 'keyframe' across src/ finds no remaining assertion of the falsified mechanism. The manifest's cycle-1 'three decisions worth defending' section (lines 29-33) still states it uncorrected, but the cycle-2 section (lines 132-141) retracts it explicitly in the same file -- recorded, not charged.

title: The no-ffmpeg degrade line reports '0s' and persists duration_s=0.0 / width=0 / height=0 / length_s=0.0 as if measured, when nothing was measured.
evidence: Executed by the checker with ffmpeg and ffprobe made unavailable (ffmpeg_available() -> False confirmed first): `ingest prep probe src_a6d5d1b66aa0` -> GREEN 'src_a6d5d1b66aa0: 0s, 1 chunk(s), 0 narration segment(s) [no ffmpeg - one chunk on the original file]', exit 0, and media.json carries duration_s 0.0, width 0, height 0 and one chunk with length_s 0.0 pointing at the original path. The one-chunk-on-the-original shape with ffmpeg_version unset is exactly what VL1 REQUIRES, and the bracketed suffix is the contract's own designated record of why -- so this is not scored as an I-VL3 violation, which targets an unqualified success claim (AT-164). But the leading '0s' is the same numeral a real zero-duration probe produces, and a downstream consumer reading media.json cannot tell 'not measured' from 'measured as zero'. Fix direction: render an unset duration as '(duration unknown - no ffprobe)' and prefer None over 0.0 for the unmeasured fields.

title: mtime_ns has ~0.5ms real granularity on this Windows host, so an idempotent write landing in the same filesystem tick as the baseline stat is still invisible - the residual of AT-186's fix, worth stating rather than assuming nanoseconds.
evidence: Checker of at185-at187-write-not-change cycle 1, measured on the host: 200 successive identical-byte writes to one file produced only 41 distinct st_mtime_ns values (min non-zero delta 479700 ns ~ 0.48 ms), and in a tight stat/write/stat loop 40 of 50 writes left st_mtime_ns UNCHANGED. So (mtime_ns, size, sha256) detects an idempotent write only when it falls outside the ~0.5 ms tick of that file's baseline stat. Not a live risk for either current test: the baseline walk stats and sha256s 1258 files before any command runs, and the observed sabotage-AX delta was 44.3 ms (1788892987910587700 -> 1788893032245811700). Filed low so the property is on the record and nobody later reads 'mtime_ns' as 'nanosecond-exact'. A strictly stronger instrument would be an OS-level write watcher or an st_ino/nlink check; neither is warranted today.

title: advice_scan resolves only constants defined in the SAME file, so AT-176's own shape one `import` away is invisible again -- and returns [] rather than any unresolved marker.

Measured by running the collector directly on constructed sources: `from autotester.stages.media_prep import PREP_COMMAND` plus the verbatim media_prep construction f"run `{PREP_COMMAND} " f"{slug} {sid}` on the HOST first" yields **[]** -- not a partial render, not a warning, nothing. Same for a name that is not module-level at all: `def f(group): raise RuntimeError(f"run `autotester {group} prep x`")` yields []. That is precisely the AT-176 blind spot this unit closed, restored by an ordinary refactor of a constant whose entire purpose is to live in one place. Not raised high: measured zero live instances (all 9 collected sites today resolve same-module) and tests/test_media_prep.py's instance test still covers require_prepared directly. Fix direction: resolve `from X import NAME` by parsing the named module's own module-level constants (the import graph inside src/autotester is small and static), or -- cheaper and strictly honest -- surface the unresolved sites so the hole has a count instead of being indistinguishable from 'no advice here' (AT-195).

title: _is_documentation covers only ast.Expr(Constant), so a bare f-string or +-concatenated documentation statement is scanned as advice -- including this codebase's own variable-docstring convention if ever written as an f-string.
evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1. tests/advice_scan.py _is_documentation() filters `isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant)`, but the same commit taught advice_in() to scan ast.JoinedStr and ast.BinOp, and a bare JoinedStr/BinOp statement is also an ast.Expr. Measured on constructed sources: f"""the old name was autotester media prep and it is dead""" as a bare statement yields ['media prep and it is dead']; "the old name was " + "autotester media prep" + " and it is dead" yields ['media prep and it is dead', 'media prep']. The sharp case is the first: PREP_COMMAND's own variable-docstring exists to record that `autotester media prep` is dead, and _is_documentation's docstring claims it 'covers real docstrings and this codebase's variable-docstring convention' -- it covers the plain-Constant form only, so documenting a dead command in the f-string form would FAIL the guard it is supposed to be exempt from. Latent, not live: walked every .py under src/autotester with ast and found ZERO bare JoinedStr/BinOp statements, so the suite is green for a real reason. Fix direction: widen the exclusion to `isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant | ast.JoinedStr | ast.BinOp)` -- one clause, same rule (an expression statement's value is discarded, so the program can never hand it to anyone).

title: The COMMAND regex takes lowercase words greedily, so a literal argument is swallowed into the 'command' the CLI oracle then checks.
evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1. tests/advice_scan.py COMMAND = r'autotester ((?:[a-z][a-z-]*)(?: [a-z][a-z-]*)*)' has no notion of where the command stops and the arguments begin. Filed so it is on the record before advice ever quotes a concrete slug. Fix direction: stop the match at the first token that is not a registered group/subcommand name, resolved from the live typer app rather than guessed.

title: UNRESOLVED prevents a wrong command being reported but is dropped silently -- 'marks it rather than pretending' overstates: an unresolvable site is indistinguishable from a file containing no advice.
evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1. tests/advice_scan.py advice_in() filters `if command and UNRESOLVED not in command` and appends nothing otherwise; advice_in_source() returns only resolved (file, command) rows. So the sentinel is a false-positive guard, not a marker -- no count, no warning, no test, nothing a human ever reads. Measured: both AT-192 shapes return [] from advice_in(), byte-identical to a file with no advice at all. The BOUNDARY itself is honestly disclosed (module docstring: 'a value that only exists at runtime stays a hole'; manifest 'What this does NOT claim'), so this is imprecision in one word rather than a false claim -- filed low, and separately from AT-192, for that reason.
