title: test_the_dialog_page_does_not_trap_the_crawl enumerates the two terminal statuses its author observed instead of asserting the invariant it is named for, so a load-induced aborted_error reds the adapter's own slot-1 verify.
evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1, folding the maker's qa/feedback-inbox.md entry. tests/test_explore_live.py:139 asserts `dialog_node.status.value in ('aborted_dialog','explored')`; NodeStatus has exactly three terminal values and the excluded third, ABORTED_ERROR, is the one a loaded host produces. CONFIRMED INTERMITTENT, NOT A REGRESSION: `git show --stat e2f119f` touches tests/ and .goal/ only -- no file under src/autotester/stages/explore* changed, so there is no code for a regression to live in -- and the checker observed 7 consecutive clean runs (3 full suites including both sabotage runs; 3 isolated runs of the file, 8 passed each; 1 isolated run executed CONCURRENTLY with a second full suite, 8 passed). Could not be reproduced even under deliberate load. RULING ON THE MAKER'S GENERALISATION: substantially right, imprecisely stated -- this test asserts membership in a TWO-element set, not 'one exact terminal NodeStatus', so the maker's wording would sweep in tests that are not brittle. The correct shape is narrower: a live test must assert the invariant it is NAMED for, not enumerate the outcomes the author happened to observe. Here 'does not trap the crawl' is already fully carried by `crawl.finished_at is not None` on the line above; whether the node aborted on the dialog or on a load-induced navigation timeout, the crawl was not trapped. EXPOSURE: `uv run pytest` is the adapter's slot-1 verify and every manifest in this project cites it, so a flaky member turns 'the suite is green' from a fact into a probability -- but the failure direction is a false FAIL on a loaded host, never a false PASS, so no verdict already given rests on it; the real cost is a maker or checker meeting an unrelated red suite and learning to re-run until green. Fix direction: assert the node reached SOME terminal status (not left pending/queued) plus finished_at, so the test fails when the crawl hangs -- the thing it exists to catch -- and not when a busy host times a navigation out.

title: adjudicate's sort key omits prompt_name, so in the SHIPPED two-prompt ensemble the merge is order-dependent -- VL4's own property, falsified, with the determinism test structurally blind to it.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 1. stages/adjudicate.py:190 sorts by (offset_s, provider_label, chunk_index). PROMPT_NAMES in stages/analyze_video.py has TWO entries, so for one model and one chunk the two prompts' observations are EQUAL under that key; Python's sort is stable, so the tie is resolved by the caller's list order. Measured: two ModelObservations identical but for prompt_name (the mapping pass carrying screens/purpose/url, the issues pass carrying an issue and a different summary) produce 2 DISTINCT contents across the 2 permutations, differing in `screens`, `journey`, `issues` AND `summary` -- i.e. every first-seen-wins merge (_merge_lists union order, `url`, `purpose`, `narration`, the summary join) inherits the caller's order. The module docstring's claim 'Given the same cached observations in any order it produces byte-identical output' is therefore false in exactly the configuration the unit ships. Not caught by tests/test_adjudicate.py::test_the_result_does_not_depend_on_input_order because every fixture there is built by obs(), which hardcodes prompt_name='video_issues_v1' -- the tie the criterion needs cannot arise in it, so 8 shuffles or 500 make no difference (checker ran 500 on the single-prompt shape: 0 mismatches). Not yet a live divergence: analyze() always appends in provider->prompt->chunk loop order, and store.list_observations() glob-sorts to the same order, so today's two producers agree. It becomes live the moment anything re-adjudicates from a differently-ordered source (T-136's scorer, a partial re-run, a provider list reordered in config) -- and the sorted() call exists precisely so that nobody has to know that. Fix direction: add prompt_name to the sort key -- (offset_s, provider_label, prompt_name, chunk_index) -- so the key is total over the tuple the cache is itself keyed on; then add a fixture to the order test in which two observations differ only in prompt_name, since that is the case the criterion is about.
checker_verdict: Independently re-verified by the checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 2 (PASS): each fix confirmed by execution AND by a targeted sabotage in an isolated `git archive HEAD` extract, anchor matched exactly once and the file re-read as changed. AT-197 sort key -> 1 failure (the two-prompt permutation test) and 500 shuffles of the real 2-model x 2-prompt x 3-chunk shape give 0 mismatches; AT-198 counters -> 2 failures, and a crippled run persists observations_used=1 / observations_expected=12 on disk; AT-199 skip_unreadable -> 1 failure, and analyze(force=True) over a corrupt cache now completes (12 calls) instead of raising; AT-200 prompt_sha256 -> 1 failure; AT-202 `fields` -> 1 failure; AT-204 duplicate-label guard -> 1 failure; AT-205 negative-second guard -> 1 failure. AT-201 and AT-203 verified by reading the shipped text. NOTE on AT-199: only the skip_unreadable half is test-evidenced -- reverting the force-before-read ORDERING alone fails 0 tests (INCONCLUSIVE, filed as AT-209).

title: A VideoAnalysis records no coverage, so an analysis built from 1 of 24 intended calls is indistinguishable from a complete one -- the zero-case guard stops exactly one step short of the claim it exists to prevent.

title: A truncated cached observation raises ValueError out of analyze() and --force cannot get past it, so the crash the cache exists to survive permanently bricks the source it was protecting.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 1. store/project_store.list_observations() -> core read_json raises ValueError on an unparseable or wrong-shaped file rather than skipping it; stages/analyze_video._cached() calls list_observations() unconditionally at the TOP of observe_chunk, BEFORE the `if cached is not None and not force` test. title: The cache key is the prompt's NAME, not its content, so editing a prompt file silently reuses answers to the previous question and nothing on disk records the mix.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 1. core/paths.source_observation() names the file '{label}__{prompt_name}__{chunk:02d}.json' and stages/analyze_video._cached() matches on provider_label + prompt_name + chunk_index. Editing src/autotester/prompts/video_issues_v1.md changes neither, so every cached chunk still hits. This project treats prompts as code by rule (CLAUDE.md: 'prompts are files, not inline strings'), and the module docstring promises a re-run is safe 'after a code change' -- which is the precise case where it is not: the resulting analysis mixes answers from the old prompt and the new one for whichever chunks happened to fail last time, with no field distinguishing them. --force fixes it but nothing tells a user they need it, and --force re-spends on every chunk rather than only the stale ones. Cost of getting this wrong is real money and a wrong answer, in the only stage that spends either. Fix direction: put a hash of the rendered prompt template (not the interpolated narration) into ModelObservation and into the cache match, so a prompt edit is a natural miss and an unchanged prompt is still a free hit. That also makes 'which prompt produced this row' answerable from the artifact.

title: video_issues_v1.md never mentions the `confidence` field while instructing the model to take every spoken remark at its word, so a weak finding has no channel to be marked weak -- and adjudicate only ever raises confidence, never lowers it.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 1, judging the prompt as a prompt. The prompt correctly forbids the three failure modes that matter -- inventing ('Report only what you can point at'; 'Anything you did not see or hear in this section'; 'return an empty list -- that is a real answer, and a normal one'), paraphrasing narration ('verbatim from the transcript below. Never paraphrase and never re-transcribe'), and adding its own offset ('Do not add any offset; the system adds the section's offset itself'). Each is independently evidenced: sabotage BN (unsliced narration) fails 2 tests and BO (dropped offset) fails 1. The false-positive risk is elsewhere. schema/observation.ObservedIssue declares `confidence: Confidence = MEDIUM`, and the prompt names screen/t_start/category/severity/title/what_is_wrong/on_screen_text/narration/origin -- but never confidence. So every issue arrives MEDIUM by default whatever the model thought, while the prompt simultaneously maximises recall of spoken remarks ('**Take them at their word.**'; a requested change 'is a real finding, not something to discard because nothing is broken') and tells the model to judge severity of the PRODUCT rather than of its own certainty. stages/adjudicate.join_issues then raises confidence to HIGH on agreement and has no path that lowers it -- and two models given the same 'take them at their word' instruction will agree on the same offhand remark, so agreement is not independent evidence here. The predicted failure at scale is a sheet of HIGH-confidence S2 rows derived from asides. Not filed high: the recall bias is DELIBERATE and justified (enums.IssueCategory records that 10/33 rows of the real ground truth were spoken change requests), no model has run this prompt yet, and T-136 is where precision gets measured. Filed so the measurement is expected rather than discovered. Fix direction: give the model the confidence field explicitly with a rule tied to evidence (spoken-and-screen -> high, a single unelaborated aside -> low), and consider requiring agreement across DIFFERENT prompts, not merely different models, before HIGH.

title: at_mmss renders a negative second as '-1:55' rather than refusing, so a bad offset reaches the tester's sheet as a plausible-looking time.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 1. stages/issues.at_mmss does `total = round(seconds); f'{total // 60:02d}:{total % 60:02d}'`; Python floor division on a negative gives -1 and 55. Negative seconds are reachable -- stages/adjudicate.shift applies `offset_s` unconditionally and nothing validates it non-negative (checker measured a -50.0 offset shifting a screen at t=10.0 to t_start=-40.0; a 1e18 offset passes through equally unremarked). Filed low because it is one guard away and has no live instance. Fix direction: constrain offset_s >= 0 on MediaChunk/ModelObservation (a Field(ge=0) in the schema, which is where every shape in this system is defined), and have at_mmss refuse rather than render a negative.

title: VideoAnalysis.observations_used/expected and is_complete reach no reader: nothing in the CLI, the exported sheet or the UI surfaces a partial analysis, so the coverage numbers discharge VL3 on disk while a human still cannot see that they are holding a fragment.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 2. AT-198's fix is real and correct -- a crippled run persists observations_used=1 / observations_expected=12 into the analysis JSON (checker measured it end to end, 2 providers x 2 prompts x 3 chunks with one provider dead and the other dying after its first call). But a repo-wide grep for `observations_used|observations_expected|is_complete` outside `media/frames.py`'s unrelated `is_complete_png` returns exactly four sites: the two schema fields, the property, and the one producer in stages/adjudicate.py:208-209. The only consumers anywhere are two tests (tests/test_adjudicate_determinism.py::test_a_partial_reading_says_how_partial_it_is and tests/test_analyze_cache.py::test_the_analysis_records_how_many_calls_it_is_missing). No CLI command prints it, stages/issues.py's 13-column export has no column and no banner for it (correctly -- the sheet's shape is the tester's), and src/autotester/ui/ never mentions it. `is_complete` is additionally a @property, so it is NOT serialised into the persisted JSON (checker confirmed 'is_complete' is absent from the analysis file's keys) -- a downstream reader must recompute it. VL3's LETTER is met ('in a field, not in a log line', and the cycle-1 verdict's own fix direction said 'the field alone discharges the criterion'), which is why this is filed rather than scored. VL3's PURPOSE -- 'a human reading the sheet is entitled to know whether it is reading a full reading or a fragment' -- is not yet realised for any human who does not open the JSON. Fix direction: print the ratio in the analyze command's completion line and, when incomplete, above the exported sheet; that is where the person who is entitled to know actually looks. Belongs with T-136, which is the first unit that computes a number against this artifact.

title: adjudicate(..., expected=None) defaults observations_expected to observations_used, so any caller other than analyze() gets an artifact that silently declares itself complete -- a default-value fallback inside the very field added to stop one.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 2. stages/adjudicate.py:209 writes `observations_expected=len(shifted) if expected is None else expected`. analyze() always passes the real product (len(providers) * len(PROMPT_NAMES) * len(prep.chunks)), so today the shipped path is honest and this is latent. But adjudicate() is a public, pure function and the stated next consumer is T-136's scorer, which re-adjudicates cached observations; a re-adjudication over a partial observation directory would produce used == expected and `is_complete is True` for a fragment -- exactly the untruth AT-198 was filed about, now with a field stating it affirmatively rather than a field being absent. The keyword is optional and the default is the one value that can never be wrong-looking. Measured: adjudicate([one_observation], 'src_1') -> observations_used=1, observations_expected=1, is_complete=True. Fix direction: make `expected` required (it has exactly one production caller, so the change costs one line), or default it to 0 -- `is_complete` already returns False on expected==0, which is the correct reading of 'nobody told me what was intended'. Filed medium: no live instance, and the honest value is supplied on the only path that ships. || CHECKER 2026-09-09 (t136-scorer cycle 1): FIXED. stages/adjudicate.py:229 now writes `observations_expected=0 if expected is None else expected`; is_complete requires expected>0 so it reads 0 as not-complete. Sabotage SJ (restore len(shifted)) in an isolated git archive HEAD extract fails exactly 1 test (test_omitting_expected_records_UNKNOWN_not_complete) -- live guard, not decorative. Sole production caller stages/analyze_video.py:181 still passes the real product; no regression. Moves to `verified` only on a later re-check.

title: The force-before-read half of the AT-199 fix is unevidenced: reverting observe_chunk to consult the cache before testing `force` fails 0 tests, because skip_unreadable alone now carries the whole crash-safety promise.

Reported INCONCLUSIVE, NOT as a vacuous guard -- the ordering IS the right shape and the manifest's claim that force is checked first is true of the shipped code. The finding is that the ordering is now redundant with, and entirely shadowed by, list_observations(skip_unreadable=True): with unreadable entries skipped, reading before the force test no longer raises, so no behaviour distinguishes the two orderings and no test can. Sabotage CC (skip_unreadable -> default) does fail 1 (test_a_half_written_observation_heals_instead_of_blocking), so VL2b's crash-safety property is genuinely evidenced -- by one mechanism, not two. Consequence: if a later change reintroduces a raise inside _cached or list_observations (a new schema field, a stricter read_json), the suite will not notice that --force has again been blocked by the cache it overrides. Fix direction: one test that corrupts a cached observation and asserts analyze(force=True) both completes AND re-requests every chunk -- the checker ran exactly that by hand and it passes (12 calls), so it is a test that exists only outside the repo.

title: scripts/score_video_issues.py:92 resolves its default project root to `D:\` (repo_root().parent.parent), so the shipped command reads D:\projects\erp\issues.jsonl -- outside the repo. evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1. `root = args.root or ProjectPaths(args.project).root.parent.parent`. Measured (.work/chk-t136/probe5.py, live tree): repo_root() = D:\autoTesting; the expression = D:\; ProjectStore('erp', D:\).paths.issues = D:\projects\erp\issues.jsonl; the correct path is D:\autoTesting\projects\erp\issues.jsonl. Consequences, in order of severity: (1) the refusal the whole manifest is built around ('project erp has no derived issues... 7 truth rows', exit 2, reproduced by the checker against the real Trainers sheet) is NOT evidence that projects/erp has no issues -- the same message and the same exit code would be produced against a fully populated project, so the maker's claim that the exit code demonstrates the scorer 'can fail for the right reason' is unsupported; (2) T-136's done_check in .goal/goal.json runs the command with NO --root and expects exit 0, so the task is structurally incapable of closing even after a vision credential arrives; (3) if D:\projects\<slug>\ ever exists (a second checkout at a different depth), the scorer silently scores a DIFFERENT project's issues against this project's truth sheet. Fix direction: `root = args.root or repo_root()` (core/paths.repo_root, already honours AUTOTESTER_ROOT for tests), plus one test that runs the done_check invocation verbatim and asserts the path opened is inside the repo.

title: stages/score.py::score is order-dependent on the issue list: `max()` returns the FIRST maximum, so a tie hands the choice to store.list_issues() file order and RECALL ITSELF moves. AT-197's class, in the module that computes the north star's number.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1. score.py:219 `best = max(candidates, key=lambda c: (c[0], -c[1]), default=None)`; candidates are built by iterating `remaining`, which is `list(issues)` = the order ProjectStore.list_issues() read them off issues.jsonl (append order). The manifest asserts 'the ordering is deterministic because candidates sort on similarity then time' -- that is true only where the pair (similarity, -seconds_apart) is unique. Measured (.work/chk-t136/probe4.py): truth rows T1='cat dog' and T2='cat dot bird' both at 10s on erp1.mp4; issues X='cat dot' and Y='cad dog' both at 10s; similarity(T1,X)=similarity(T1,Y)=0.8, similarity(T2,X)=0.8, similarity(T2,Y)=0.6. With --threshold 0.7, issue order [X,Y] -> recall 0.5, order [Y,X] -> recall 1.0. At the default threshold 0.30 the recall coincides but the CLAIM does not: probe2 case B shows the per_row entry for T1 naming issue X or Y purely by list order, so `matched_title` and `similarity` in the JSON report are order-dependent under the shipped defaults. Ties are reachable in the shipped system: the ensemble is two models x two prompts and join_issues merges only within a window, so near-duplicate reports at the same second are exactly what it produces. This is the defect class that cost T-133 a fix cycle (AT-197: a sort key with ties handing the decision to caller order) and that VL4 was tightened for; the scorer is the module where it costs a number a human is asked to trust. Fix direction: make the candidate key total (append the issue id as a final tiebreak), or sort `remaining` on a content key before matching -- and pin it with a permutation test over the shipped shape, the way test_adjudicate_determinism.py does for VL4.

title: scripts/score_video_issues.py::coverage skips a contributing source whose analysis is absent from disk, so `complete: true` is reachable while a scored source's reading is entirely unknown -- AT-207's own untruth, reintroduced at source granularity inside AT-207's fix.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1. coverage() line 53-54: `analysis = store.load_analysis(source_id); if analysis is None: continue` -- the source contributes issues to the score but nothing to the coverage totals, and `complete` is computed as `not partial and expected > 0` over the sources that happened to load. Measured end to end (.work/chk-t136/probe7.py, temp root, real ProjectStore/JSON files): two sources each contributing one issue, analysis.json saved for source 1 only (used=4/expected=4), one truth row -> exit 0 and coverage {observations_used: 4, observations_expected: 4, complete: true, partial_sources: []}. Source 2's reading is not partial and not zero -- it is unknown -- and the report affirmatively states the run was complete. AT-207 was filed because 'a recall from 1 of 12 model calls is otherwise indistinguishable from one taken from 12 of 12'; a missing analysis is the same indistinguishability one level up, and the manifest claims this unit 'names partial sources and says whether the run was complete'. The maker did get the all-zero case right: with no analysis at all, expected=0 and complete is False (measured). Fix direction: count sources without an analysis into a third list (e.g. `sources_without_analysis`) and let any entry in it force `complete: false` -- silence is not coverage.

title: recording_key splits on the first '(' and falls back to the raw cell, so distinct recordings collapse to one key (`clip (1).mp4` and `clip (2).mp4` both -> `clip`) and an empty/None cell becomes `''`, which is matchable -- two unknown recordings score as the same recording.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1, measured directly (.work/chk-t136/probe1.py): 'clip (1).mp4' -> 'clip'; 'clip (2).mp4' -> 'clip'; 'erp (final) cut.mp4' -> 'erp'; 'report (v2).mp4 (Divya)' -> 'report'; '' -> ''; None -> ''; '  ' -> ''; 0 -> ''. `clip (N).ext` is the exact name Windows and Chrome give a duplicate file, so the collision is not exotic. The absence case is the sharper one: unlike the `At` column -- where the maker correctly refuses an unparseable cell BECAUSE second zero 'matches whatever happens to open the recording' -- a blank recording cell is accepted silently and produces a key that CAN match. Measured end to end (.work/chk-t136/probe6.py, temp root): a truth sheet whose Clip column is empty in every row, scored against two issues with an empty recording_label, exits 0 with recall 1.0, found 2, false_positives 0. The same sheet against issues on a real clip exits 0 with recall 0.0 -- the maker's own stated design principle is that a fact which 'silently yields a recall of zero' must be enforced in code rather than remembered, and the recording column is the one input where it is not. Fix direction: refuse a blank recording cell the way at_seconds refuses a blank At, and key on the leading token only when it looks like a filename (an extension) rather than on everything before the first parenthesis.

title: Every real Gemini call 400'd: the Pydantic response_schema carries additionalProperties (from this repo's own C1 extra=forbid) and $defs, neither of which Gemini's dialect accepts. The T-131 provider unit was checker-PASSed against a FAKE client that accepted any config.
evidence: First real vision call, 2026-09-09. `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: Unknown name "additional_properties" at 'generation_config.response_schema'` x5 occurrences. providers/gemini.py:74 passed the Pydantic class straight to response_schema; google-genai renders extra=forbid as additionalProperties:false and nests $defs/$ref, and Gemini's schema dialect (an OpenAPI 3.0 subset) has neither. Every observe_chunk call raised ProviderError, analyze() raised NoObservations, and the refusal text blamed missing credentials -- which were present and valid.
expected: A seam whose only job is talking to a third-party API cannot be proven by a double that agrees with us. Sanitise the schema (providers/gemini_schema.py) and validate the returned dict on our side.
note: Three distinct defects surfaced in the first 60 seconds of real use, each invisible to the fake client: additionalProperties/$defs; a depth guard that counted structural nesting instead of $ref expansion and refused a valid schema; and DROPPED_KEYS deleting ObservedIssue.title -- a real field sharing a name with a JSON-Schema annotation -- which made Gemini answer 'required[3]: property is not defined'.
reopen_reason: Sweep 2026-09-09 corrected twice in ~10 minutes, disclosed rather than hidden. First: reopened verified->open after independently reproducing a peer checker's FAIL (C5, gemini.py:142's response validation unguarded -- sabotage-confirmed by me in my own isolated extract, 910 passed / 0 failed with it removed). Second, on rereading the peer's own reconciliation more carefully: they explicitly reasoned 'I would have left it fixed rather than upgrading it on a FAILing unit -- the defect itself is genuinely closed and I proved it independently, but upgrading a row while the unit is FAILing is the claim-outrunning-check shape the sweep exists to catch.' That is more precise than my blunt open: AT-230's own defect (the request schema causing every real call to 400) IS closed and sabotage-proven by BOTH checkers (FF: reverting gemini.py:79 fails exactly one test, in both our independent extracts). What is NOT verified is the whole unit, because C5 (a criterion the manifest itself requested) is unguarded -- tracked separately now as AT-266, not as part of AT-230's own scope. status=fixed matches that: closed with evidence, not yet independently confirmed as a fully passing unit. See qa/verdicts/at230-gemini-schema.md (restored to the peer's own INDEPENDENT CONCURRENT CHECK reconciliation, which I briefly overwrote by the exact mistake I had just corrected once already this session, then restored byte-intact).

title: The two-prompt pass reports each fault TWICE and adjudicate does not merge the pair, roughly doubling the false-positive count on the first real run.
evidence: First real reading, 6 issues from 3 recordings, and they are 3 distinct faults each reported twice: erp1 'Rule T3 validation error prevents stage transition' (13s) + 'Rule T3 validation error blocks moving trainer to next stage' (16s), both category=validation; erp2 'Incorrect document type option' + 'Document type dropdown option should be CITS Certificate instead of CIPSA' (both 1s, copy_text); erp3 'Home Location field presents training centers instead of personal location' + 'Home location field misuse' (both 2s, wrong_model). join_issues merges on same screen + same category + <=SEAM_WINDOW_S; the erp2 and erp3 pairs share category AND timestamp and still did not merge, so the screen names must differ between the two prompts' outputs. Scored result: 6 reported, 1 matched, 5 false positives -- at least 3 of those 5 are duplicates of another reported issue, not independent wrong findings.
expected: One fault reported by two prompts of the SAME model is one fault. Either normalise the screen name before keying, or merge on (category, |dt|<=window) when the model label is identical.
note: This is the ensemble's central premise -- agreement raises confidence -- inverted: agreement currently doubles the noise instead.
checker_note: Cycle 1 checker: the merge bound and length-preference fix are sabotage-confirmed correct (both dedicated mutations reproduced exactly). Cycle verdict is FAIL for a different reason (AT-269 -- the manifest's own supporting real-world-impact narrative misattributes the mechanism), which does not implicate this fix's correctness. title: The 0.30 SequenceMatcher threshold under-counts real matches because the human writes 200 words and the model writes 20 -- length asymmetry crushes the ratio.
evidence: E-03 ('Home location' offers centres only, so a trainer's actual home town cannot be recorded -- plus a ~200-word what_is_wrong) vs our erp3 issue 'Home Location field presents training centers instead of personal location'. SAME recording, 2s apart (well inside the 20s window), semantically the same fault -- scored a MISS. The only match that scored, E-02, did so at similarity 0.37, barely over the 0.30 floor. Reported recall 1/7 = 0.143; by reading, at least 2 of 7 are genuinely found.
expected: A ratio over title+what_is_wrong penalises the model for being terser than the human. Consider matching on title alone, a containment/token-overlap measure rather than SequenceMatcher, or scoring the two fields separately.
note: The scorer is currently pessimistic about its own pipeline, which is the safer direction to be wrong in but still wrong. The number to fix before quoting recall as a capability measure.

title: A near-miss and a no-candidate-at-all are indistinguishable in the scorer's report: Match discards the rejected best candidate, so both print sim=0.00 dt=None.
evidence: stages/score.py: when `best is None or best[0] < threshold` the code appends `Match(truth=row)` with the default similarity 0.0 and seconds_apart None, throwing away the candidate it just rejected. In the first real run E-03 showed `sim=0.00 dt=None` and I read that as 'nothing was near it' -- the truth was that a candidate 2 seconds away scored just under threshold. The one field a human needs to tune --threshold is the one discarded.
expected: Record the best rejected candidate and its score on the Match, and print it in per_row. A reader tuning the threshold cannot do it blind.
note: Directly cost me a wrong reading of the first real result until I compared the two lists by hand.

title: gemini_schema is a DENY-list against four keywords that have already 400'd; the dialect is an allow-list of 24, and const / prefixItems / oneOf / allOf pass through untouched to Google

title: _already_past_login (AT-226's own fix, explore.py:118-122) swallows every exception with a bare except and returns False -- unlike its sibling _seed 15 lines below (AT-098) which names and stores the exception
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore.py:115-123. try: rt.session.goto(login_url); rt.session.settle(...) / except Exception: return False -- no `as exc`, nothing logged, nothing stored on rt. Compare _seed at :136-145 (same file, same commit era, AT-098's own fix) which distinguishes NavigationRefused from other Exception and records the message in rt.seed_error precisely so an operator can tell a domain refusal from a DNS timeout from a genuine 'not authenticated'. _already_past_login's caller (line 108-110) treats any exception here identically to 'the app did not redirect -- not authenticated', then falls through to run_case(case, rt.session), which calls goto again on the same URL. A transient nav failure (timeout, DNS blip, NavigationRefused) during this precheck is silently reclassified as ordinary not-yet-authenticated, so if the same condition recurs inside run_case the crawl can still hit the guaranteed step-timeout AT-226 exists to avoid -- with no signal anywhere that the precheck itself failed rather than genuinely observed no-redirect.

title: test_a_login_page_that_does_not_redirect_still_runs_the_case is vacuous against an always-skip regression: it never asserts the login FILL step actually ran
evidence: tests/test_explore_login_bypass.py:55-65 only asserts crawl.status is CrawlStatus.COMPLETED and stop_reason == 'frontier empty'. Sabotage-confirmed in an isolated git-archive extract (uv-synced venv, __file__ resolved inside the extract): replaced _already_past_login's body with 'return True' (always report already-past-login, i.e. always skip the login case including when it genuinely needs to run) -- all 22 tests in tests/test_explore_login_bypass.py + tests/test_explore.py still pass, including this one. The fake site's SITE dict makes BASE (post-skip) and the post-fill destination structurally identical for crawl purposes, so 'the crawl completed' cannot distinguish 'the case ran and filled the field' from 'the case was never attempted'. Direction (a) sabotage (return False, never skip) correctly fails the redirect test as the manifest and prior verdict f718273 both show; direction (b) (always skip) was not tested by the manifest and is not caught by any existing assertion.
checker_note: Contract explore.md's requested AT-226 criterion 'A login case whose NAVIGATE target does NOT redirect still runs normally' is therefore NOT genuinely evidenced -- current code is correct (read directly: the guard is a real path comparison, not a stub), but a future regression that made _already_past_login always return True would ship undetected. title: AT-276 introduces its OWN false-positive mode: stopwording content-bearing action words can strip a short bug report down to near-nothing, inflating similarity() to 1.0 for genuinely unrelated faults
evidence: src/autotester/stages/similarity_score.py similarity(). Mechanism: containment = |shorter & longer| / |shorter|; a word removed from STOPWORDS that occurred ONLY in the shorter text shrinks the denominator without shrinking the numerator, which can only raise the score. AT-232 (33 words) was purely grammatical/domain boilerplate (field/validation/screen/edit); AT-276 added many CONTENT-bearing action words (export/downloads/corrupted/when/large/count/update/filter/message/change...) that can legitimately be the entire distinguishing content of a short report. Constructed pair, reproduced in isolated git-archive extract: "Certificate export downloads corrupted when large" vs "Certificate generation crashes when the network is slow" -- two genuinely unrelated faults (data-corruption-on-export vs infra/network crash). Under AT-232-only STOPWORDS: 0.3333 (below threshold, correctly rejected). Under AT-276 STOPWORDS (this unit): 1.0 -- every word in the shorter sentence except "certificate" is now stripped (export/downloads/corrupted/when/large all newly stopworded), leaving shorter={"certificate"}, shared={"certificate"}, ratio 1/1. Second pair confirms the same mechanism: "Trainer count updates wrong after filter change" vs "Trainer profile photo fails to render after refresh" goes from 0.2857 (old) to 1.0 (new). This is not the same false-positive AT-276 fixed -- it is a NEW, more severe (score-ceiling) instance the fix itself introduces, on constructed pairs outside the 6 AT-276 was measured against.
expected: Not a blocker for AT-276 (it is not asked to be complete, and the two real corpus matches + AT-232 boilerplate case still hold). Worth a follow-up before STOPWORDS is extended a third time: consider guarding against near-total stopword erosion of the SHORTER text (e.g. refuse/flag when the shorter word set drops below N words after filtering, since a 1-word match is definitionally unfalsifiable) rather than adding more words to a list whose growth increasingly risks this exact failure mode.
checker_note: Filed during Mode A check of at276-stopwords-second-tranche (cycle 1), per the checker dispatch instruction to press specifically on whether this second STOPWORDS extension introduced its own false-positive risk. Does not block PASS: AT-276 is judged on its own stated scope and delivers it, sabotage-confirmed independently; this is a structural risk in the containment metric that STOPWORDS-list growth makes worse, disclosed here for the next fix cycle rather than argued into this one. Cycle-2 checker reproduced the real score-path fix at cbdfab1; weakening the two-shared-token gate produced the original two 1.0 false matches and both AT-279 contradictory matches.

title: The two-word distinctiveness floor makes short-title scoring internally inconsistent: exact one-token reports are forced misses while one shared token in a contradictory two-token pair is accepted

title: url_template is not idempotent across the keep_host boundary, so every screen learned from a VIDEO was invisible to coverage and its routes looked permanently unknown
evidence: core/urls.py's own docstring promised `url_template(url_template(u)) == url_template(u)`. Reproduced against production code before the fix: url_template('https://demo.test/students/42') -> 'demo.test/students/{id}' (what stages/ingest.py stores, per ingest.md I7), and url_template of THAT with keep_host=False -> '/demo.test/students/{id}', while the observed URL reduces to '/students/{id}'. stages/coverage.py::_known_paths re-templates every stored url_pattern exactly that way, so a FlowSpec containing a screen for precisely the URL a run visited still reported a CoverageGap ['/students/{id}']. Cycle 2 deletes the heuristic and canonicalises all four producers to keep_host=False; re-templating a path is idempotent with no guessing. The docstring's defence is 'the caller KNOWS the string is an absolute url, because it came out of an address bar', and prompts/ingest_video_v1.md does support it ('Record the URL only when the address bar is legible on screen. title: Three fail-safe guards in known_hosts survive deletion with the whole suite green, including the ValueError guard the manifest names as part of the AT-301/302 fix

Each guard is also load-bearing: without it an exception escapes known_hosts and aborts the entire scan() walk mid-migration, and N11's arm is exercised on real data every time a json file resolves to the root fallback. title: _project_dir_of's root-containment bound is undefended by any test and is a LEXICAL comparison, so a relative root with absolute paths walks above the root
evidence: Checker's own mutation N2 against 8d30823: deleting `if parent == root: break` from _project_dir_of leaves all 21 tests green, so nothing defends the containment bound in a repo whose AT-149/AT-150 history is exactly path containment. Probed directly, the bound is also lexical rather than resolved: with a project.json in <tmp>/outer declaring evil.test and an artifact at <tmp>/outer/inner/screenmap.json, _project_dir_of(<abs artifact>, Path('inner')) returns <tmp>/outer - it climbs ABOVE the intended root and adopts a foreign project's hosts, which under --write would strip a real first path segment. Reachability stated honestly: NOT reachable through main(), because scan() iterates root.rglob(), which yields paths in the same relative/absolute form as root and keeps the comparison consistent - scan(Path('inner')) on that same tree correctly returns {}, and the properly-formed absolute case is contained (returns root, known_hosts set(), scan {}). A latent robustness gap in a helper, not a live escape.

title: AT-302 is a knowingly PARTIAL fix: a genuinely mangled IPv6 pattern is still not repaired, because hosts are stored bracketless and the mangled pattern is bracketed

So the false-positive half of AT-302 is genuinely fixed ('[' is no longer a declared host) and the true-positive half is not implemented. No live impact: no project declares an IPv6 base_url, and the failure direction is under-repair (stale display), never corruption.

title: KILLED is still exit != 0: a mutation causing a COLLECTION ERROR is reported KILLED with an empty failure list, and the 'defends:' label is never asserted
evidence: Checker's own probe D against the harness as committed at 6cc11e6, run from the real repo. Baseline asserted green (21 passed, exit 0); the mutation set was replaced with one that injects a syntax error into scripts/migrate_url_patterns.py in the copy. So `verdict = "KILLED" if code != 0` cannot distinguish (a) the test named for the fix failed, (b) an unrelated test failed - the AT-196 flake landing mid-run rather than at baseline, (c) the suite failed to collect. Corroborated inside the committed harness itself: M4's `defends:` string names test_a_file_nested_below_the_project_is_still_judged_by_it, and `grep -c 'def test_a_file_nested_below_the_project_is_still_judged_by_it' tests/test_migrate_url_patterns.py` returns 0 - the test does not exist. The harness printed the wrong name confidently on four consecutive kills because nothing ever compares that string to the run.

Every failure mode above produces a false KILLED -> false non-vacuous -> false PASS, which is the direction the whole C7 clause family exists to close: AT-307 shut 'already red BEFORE the mutation'; this is 'red for the wrong reason AFTER it'. title: An EMPTY `kills` list makes scripts/mutation_check.py report an unattributed kill - the AT-311 defect, reachable in the instrument built to close it
evidence: Checker's own attack against 55efeac. `killed = code == 1 and not survivors`; with `kills: []`, `expected` is empty so `survivors` is always empty and the verdict degenerates to `code == 1` - 'some test in the selection failed'. title: A mutation can escape the sandbox: an absolute or ../ `file` path makes scripts/mutation_check.py write OUTSIDE its copytree
evidence: Checker's own attack against 55efeac. `target = work / mutation['file']` performs no containment check, and pathlib join semantics DISCARD `work` for an absolute path: work / 'C:/.../victim.py' -> 'C:/.../victim.py'; work / '../../x.py' -> the temp root. Driven end to end: with an absolute `file`, the harness read, mutated and rewrote a decoy file outside the sandbox, then reported killed=False exit=0 because the mutation landed where the sandboxed suite never imports (a false SURVIVED plus a live-tree write). A ../../ path onto an EXISTING outside file did the same; onto a nonexistent one it raises a bare FileNotFoundError rather than a MutationError, so the run dies with an unhandled traceback instead of a refusal. This falsifies two stated claims: _sandbox's docstring ('so a mutation can never touch the live tree') and the manifest's 'Mutations run in a copytree OUTSIDE the repo'. tests/test_the_live_tree_is_never_touched does not catch it - it only exercises a well-formed relative path. Certification direction is safe (false SURVIVED, never false KILLED); damage direction is not - a live file is rewritten, and if the process dies between the mutation write and the restore it stays mutated. In a repo whose AT-149/AT-150 history is path containment, this is the finding that most deserves a test.
expected: target = (work / mutation['file']).resolve(); refuse unless work.resolve() is among its parents. One line each, and the mutation that kills the new test writes itself.

The absolute-path decoy was given CRLF content on purpose so that a write-and-restore would show as a hash change even where a text comparison would not (AT-316's blind spot), and its sha256 is IDENTICAL before and after (3c3130ae81b2fe35...) - byte-unchanged, not merely 'an error was raised'. Additionally probed a symlink inside the sandbox pointing out: copytree follows it and copies the content as a regular file, so the mutation lands in the copy and the outside victim is byte-unchanged. Defending mutation (sandbox containment removed) killed by both escape tests.

title: FIVE duplicate ids in qa/issues.jsonl, each naming two DIFFERENT findings - the checker's own ledger violates 'ids sequential, never reused'
evidence: Found at 55efeac while appending this check's rows; PRE-EXISTING, so not chargeable to at311-mutation-check - verified by re-reading `git show HEAD:qa/issues.jsonl`, where the collisions are already present. AT-282, AT-288, AT-289, AT-290 and AT-291 each appear twice, and in every case the two rows are NOT identical (no harmless double-append): AT-288 is 'T-135 regressed autotester doctor' vs 't135 breaks the repo's own C2 architecture-budget'; AT-289 'Only the CLI video seam closes VideoRequests' vs 'resolve_requests is wired to the CLI merge'; AT-290 'A merge can never teach a url_pattern' vs "AT-287's blast radius, measured rather than..."; AT-291 'resolve_requests closes and attributes requests' vs 'url_template is STILL not idempotent'; AT-282 two different framings of the adapter's literal verify commands. Root cause worth confirming: all five sit in the AT-282..AT-291 band, which suggests two sessions appending against the same tail rather than five independent slips.

title: A `kills` NAME is not a unique test identifier: scripts/mutation_check.py attributes a kill to a same-named test in a DIFFERENT file or class
evidence: Checker's own attack against 2ac4c21. collected_tests() returns line.split('::')[-1] and failed_tests() returns nodeid.split('::')[-1]; both discard the file and the class, so the attribution check compares BARE FUNCTION NAMES. Within-file variant confirmed too: two classes in one file both yield 'test_method', so TestB::test_method failing satisfies a kills claiming TestA::test_method (failed: ['test_big_values_are_big','test_method'], killed=True). title: 'A mutation cannot reach the exit-code clause' is false, and it is asserted in a committed docstring, a committed test comment and the manifest
evidence:
Checker's own attack against 2ac4c21, testing the cycle-2 argument rather than accepting it. The claim (manifest, scripts/mutation_check.py is_kill.__doc__, and tests/test_mutation_check.py's AT-315 comment block) is that a weakened `exit_code != 0` survives EVERY possible mutation, because a collection error yields no FAILED lines so `expected <= failures` fails too. The premise silently assumes every non-1 non-zero exit is a COLLECTION error. pytest exit 2 is INTERRUPTED, and an interrupted run prints the FAILED lines of tests that already failed. One anchor, one replacement, on the unit's own synthetic fixture: old='    if value > 10:
        return "big"
    return "small"
' new='    if value > 10:
        return "small"
    raise KeyboardInterrupt
', kills=['test_big_values_are_big']. Committed check() returns {'killed': False, 'exit': 2, 'expected': ['test_big_values_are_big'], 'failed': ['test_big_values_are_big'], 'survivors': []}. expected <= failures HOLDS at exit 2: weakened `exit_code != 0` -> True (killed), correct `exit_code == 1` -> False. RULING on the general rule proposed for later units ('when a property cannot be reached by mutation, extract it until it can be asserted directly'): NOT confirmed. Sound as a last resort, and not forbidden, but the standard of proof used here must not carry forward - 'I could not think of a mutation' is not 'no mutation exists', and this is the second confident unreachability claim from this pair falsified by one attempt. No contract amendment made: C7's existing 'mutate the specific branch it claims to defend' already demands the search, and a contract is not amended against a pending verdict. If the maker wants the rule in C7 it comes as its own feedback-inbox entry, with the burden stated - an unreachability claim must name the state space it searched and why that search is exhaustive. Here the space was pytest's exit codes, and 2 was never considered.

title: collected_nothing is True for pytest exit 2, so the report says 'pytest ran nothing' about a run in which tests ran and one failed
evidence: Checker's own attack against 2ac4c21, a by-product of the AT-321 reproduction. collected_nothing is `code in (NO_TESTS_RAN, 2, 3, 4)`. pytest exit 2 is INTERRUPTED, not a collection failure: the exit-2 mutation above ran two tests, one FAILED with a real assertion error and its name appears in the FAILED lines, and the field still reads True - so report() prints 'NOTE: that exit code means pytest ran nothing - not a kill' about a run that demonstrably ran tests. The field is ADVISORY only (it never affects `killed`, and is_kill's exit_code == 1 correctly holds the line), so this is a false statement in output, not a false verdict - hence low, and not a FAIL line. It supersedes half of the cycle-1 ruling on the manifest's judgement #3: the grouping is right for `killed`, the stated justification ('no test result was produced') is false for 2.

title: report() labels any survivor 'vacuous for its property' - the exact phrasing C7's zero-failure clause forbids on that evidence alone
evidence: Read at 2ac4c21. report() prints, for ANY survival, `SURVIVING      : <name>  <- vacuous for its property`. C7's 2026-09-08 zero-failure clause says: 'anchor matched once' + 'file changed' are necessary but NOT sufficient, because an anchor can match once inside a comment, a docstring, or a line no test exercises; 'When a sabotage yields 0 failures the harness must report it as INCONCLUSIVE - mutation not shown to change behaviour ... It must never be reported as "the guard test is vacuous" on that evidence alone.' The instrument's anchor-count and changed-nothing refusals supply exactly the necessary half and nothing more, then draws the forbidden conclusion. The clause exists because a checker's sabotage U in at151-at152-both-arms matched once, changed the file and produced 0 failures on a line no assertion reads; and because of AT-140 cycle 1, where a no-op sabotage read as 'my test is vacuous' and the maker nearly rewrote a correct test. C7's 2026-09-11 mutation duty makes this instrument the mandated route for every test-adding unit, which is precisely where that wording does the most damage.

The stronger form, if wanted later, is to have the survivor branch say what would upgrade it (revert the actual fix hunk rather than a nearby string), which is the remedy C7 names.
